For example, if a trade is executed at 10 AM at a level of 25 bps, given a deal spread of 40, the 25 bps is the strike spread. At the end of the day, the markets could close at around 30. all quotes.description: Time Weighted Average Bid Ask Spread Percentage
all quotes.documentation:
Provides the time weighted average of all bid/ask spreads as a percentage of the mid price. The bid/ask points used for the computation correspond to the quotes received for the period indicated by Calc Interval (PX393, CALC_INTERVAL) (default value is five days, supports from 1D up to 90D) ending in the complete trading day prior to the date indicated by End Date Override (PX392, END_DATE_OVERRIDE) (default value is latest completed trading day). Partial trading days are excluded from the average. Bid/ask spread points are only considered during the continuous trading period, and only when the spread is defined and non-negative.

Equities
Each BID or ASK quote persists until a cancellation tick is received. For spread derivation, only complete quotes are considered. Negative spread and missing quotes are excluded from the calculation.

FX
An appropriate stream (BGNE, BGN, etc.) is used to derive Bid-Ask spread. When multiple quotes have the same timestamp, the volume-weighted average is used to derive the representative quote for each side. The spread is then averaged over the requested interval with seconds' precision. Negative spread and incomplete quotes are excluded from the calculation.

all quotes.description: VWAP Volume for All Order Book Trades
all quotes.documentation:
Volume corresponding to VWAP (Volume Weighted Average Price) for Automated Trades (PQ715, VWAP_AUTOMATED). VWAP for Automated Trades is a trading benchmark calculated by adding up the values of all order book (electronic) trade transactions (price times shares traded) and then dividing by the total shares traded for the time period.

This field can be used in conjunction with the VWAP Start Time (PR313, VWAP_START_TIME), VWAP End Time (PR314, VWAP_END_TIME), VWAP Start Date (PR470, VWAP_START_DT), VWAP End Date (PR471, VWAP_END_DT), VWAP Date (PR315, VWAP_DT), VWAP Minimum Price (PR951, VWAP_MIN_PX), VWAP Maximum Price (PR952, VWAP_MAX_PX), VWAP Minimum Size (PR953, VWAP_MIN_SIZE) and VWAP Maximum Size (PR954, VWAP_MAX_SIZE) overrides.

The calculation excludes any manual trade apart from off-exchange trades, non-trade price quotes like Opening Price, Official Close, Index Point, Aver Price Trade, Current Inside Match Price, NASDAQ First Trade Actual, Far Indicative Clearing Price, Intraday Trade Detail, Market Center Official Close, Near Indicative Clearing Price, and NASDAQ Official Opening Price from VWAP calculations.

Tokyo Stock Exchange (JT/JO/JQ)

It is not presently available on the Japanese Composite (JP) or the following proprietary trading systems (PTSs):
Chi-X Japan (JI)
SBI Japannext (JE)
SBI Japannext X Market (JU)

The Japanese Evaluation Price is calculated intraday and is derived as follows, listed in order of priority (1 being the highest priority). If a higher priority value is not available, then the next value in the priority order will be evaluated.
   1. The Exchange Base Price published after market close (current day only, after the close of the afternoon trading session).
   2. The Last Trade (current day only), unless there is a more recent Special or Continuous Quote (bid/ask) available.
   3. The Exchange Base Price published before market close (before the close of the afternoon trading session). This may be the Exchange Base Price that is published before market open.
   4. The most recent Japanese Evaluation Price from a prior trading day (most likely derived from the previous relevant evening's Exchange Base Price, per priority [1] above).

"After market close" and "before market close" both refer to the close of the afternoon trading session only. For the purposes of the Japanese Evaluation Price calculation, the afternoon trading session is considered a continuation of the morning trading session

Provides the basic Earnings Per Share (EPS) that is the portion of a company's profit allocated to each common shareholder. It is calculated as net income available to common shareholders divided by the basic weighted average number of shares outstanding for the period. This field returns bottom-line EPS based on the setting for 'Non-GAAP Adjustments' in Fundamental Analysis Defaults. The field FA Adjusted Financials Override (DT094, FA_ADJUSTED) can be set to 'Y' to return adjusted data for excluding abnormal items. Unit: Actual

Brazil:
For Brazil EPS is computed based on the quotation lot of the company, refer to Quote Lot Size (PR091, PX_QUOTE_LOT_SIZE) for the quotation lot.

INDEX
For equity indices the EPS is an index-level aggregate of all equity contributions. Each equity contribution is calculated as:

  (EPS × Shares × FX) / (Index Divisor × Coverage Factor)

Where:
  EPS is Basic Earnings per Share (IS061, IS_EPS).
  Shares are the number of shares of a security in the index. Refer to Member Weightings (MEMB).
  FX is the foreign exchange rate applied for securities that have a different fundamental currency,
  refer to Currency Override (DS215, EQY_FUND_CRNCY).
  The index divisor is Divisor (IN018, INDX_DIVISOR).
  Coverage factor is further defined as 1 - (Unused Market Cap / Index Market Cap).
  Where:
    Unused market cap is the sum of a securities' market cap that does not have an equity contribution to the index value.
    Index market cap is the sum of a securities' market cap. Market cap is the latest price for the security Last Price (PR005, PX_LAST)
    multiplied by the number of shares outstanding in Basic Weighted Average Number of Shares (IS060,IS_AVG_NUM_SH_FOR_EPS).

With the exceptions described below, the Official Close is an exchange-calculated and published closing price. Depending on the methodology that is used by the exchange, the closing price may differ from the last traded price.

For the Swiss Stock Exchange (Exchange Codes or Feed Sources of "SE", "SW" and "VX") that have not traded on the current trading day, the field will reflect the value of the most recent official close for that security. This may differ from the Bloomberg Close Price (Q1131, BLOOMBERG_CLOSE_PRICE_RT), which includes reference price ('ref') updates for illiquid securities on days when there are no trades.

For equities, exchange traded funds (ETFs) and convertible bonds admitted for trading on the Japanese stock exchanges (Exchange Codes or Feed Sources of "JF", "JN", "JS" and "JT") the field provides a Bloomberg deriving closing price, which is determined as follows. This algorithm has been formed in conjunction with Tokyo Stock Exchange.
- When the market closes with a trade bearing a Bloomberg condition code value of 'e' (Closing Price), the price of that trade will form the closing price for the day.
- When the market closes with a trade bearing a Bloomberg condition code value of 'z' (Zaraba-Bike) or 'AE' (AM Closing Price) and the market (represented via a Bloomberg bid/ask condition code value) is not in a 'SPEC' (Special Quotation) or 'CONE' (Continuous Quote) state at the closing auction, the 'z' or 'AE' trade price will form the closing price for the day.
- When the market closes with a trade bearing a Bloomberg condition code value of 'z' (Zaraba-Bike) or 'AE' (AM Closing Price) and the market (represented via a Bloomberg bid/ask condition code value) is in 'SPEC' (Special Quotation) or 'CONE' (Continuous Quote) state at the closing auction, the 'SPEC' or 'CONE' bid or ask price will form the closing price for the day.
- When there are no trades at all for the entire trading day, and the market (represented via a Bloomberg bid/ask condition code value) is not in 'SPEC' (Special Quotation) or 'CONE' (Continuous Quote) state at the closing auction, the closing price will be empty/blank.
- When there are no trades at all for the entire trading day, but the market (represented via a Bloomberg bid/ask condition code value) is in 'SPEC' (Special Quotation) or 'CONE' (Continuous Quote) state at the closing auction, the 'SPEC' or 'CONE' bid or ask price will form the closing price for the day. 

On the Bloomberg European Composite (Exchange Code or Feed Source of "EU"), the field provides the Bloomberg Official Close, derived from the last eligible trade from the highest ranked markets that have reported a trade on that day. Markets are ranked according to their market models. Immediate executions (trades) from automatic execution venues are prioritised over manual trades reported from quote-driven markets or manual trade reporting venues. Over-the-counter (OTC) venues, or manual trade reporting venues that are classed as Tier 2 contributors to the European Composite, are not eligible to contribute to the Bloomberg Official Close; only regulated markets and multilateral trading facilities (the Tier 1 contributors) are eligible. The venues that make up the Tier 1 and Tier 2 contributors will vary depending on where the instrument is admitted for trading. A Tier 1 venue may have been classed by Bloomberg as ineligible to contribute to the Bloomberg Official Close owing to extraordinary trading hours, such as a late market close time.

The Japanese Evaluation Price is calculated intraday and is derived as follows, listed in order of priority (1 being the highest priority). If a higher priority value is not available, then the next value in the priority order will be evaluated.
   1. The Exchange Base Price published after market close (current day only, after the close of the afternoon trading session).
   2. The Last Trade (current day only), unless there is a more recent Special or Continuous Quote (bid/ask) available.
   3. The Exchange Base Price published before market close (before the close of the afternoon trading session). This may be the Exchange Base Price that is published before market open.
   4. The most recent Japanese Evaluation Price from a prior trading day (most likely derived from the previous relevant evening's Exchange Base Price, per priority [1] above).

"After market close" and "before market close" both refer to the close of the afternoon trading session only. For the purposes of the Japanese Evaluation Price calculation, the afternoon trading session is considered a continuation of the morning trading session.

The equivalent field on BPOD is Summary.Price.Evaluation.

The Last Trade is available in Last Trade (PR088, PX_LAST_ACTUAL), Last Trade (RQ088, LAST_TRADE), and Summary.Price.Last.Trade (on BPOD).  The Special or Continuous Quotes are bids or asks with a condition code mnemonic of "SPEC" (special quote) or "CONE" (continuous quote).

Provides a daily volume (quantity) metric produced by Bloomberg’s Liquidity Assessment solution (LQA) for the selected security. The specific definition and calculation of this field differs by asset class.

Fixed Income:
Estimated notional that a single firm could sell in 1-day in a single trade within the current LQA Bid-Ask Spread (PY273, LQA_BID_ASK_SPREAD). The LQA model utilizes several reference data features (ex: amount outstanding, maturity, coupon), market data features (ex: number of trades, number of dealers providing executable quotes) and pricing features (ex: bid-ask spread, and price volatility) to perform a daily calculation of the expected daily volume. The value is displayed as a notional amount in the issue currency.

Provides only an estimated volume based on the constraints described above. For actual trade volumes, refer to LQA Empirical Total Trade Volume (PY585, LQA_EMPIRICAL_TOTAL_TRADE_VOLUME).

Equity and ExchangeTradedProduct:
20-day average Aggregated Share Volume (PY438, AGGREGATED_SHARE_VOLUME) across all exchanges and venues (includes Over-the-Counter (OTC) volumes), representing the total trading volume. The value is displayed as the quantity of shares.

In-the-Money Convertible Bonds:
For convertible bonds where the Convertible Model Delta S (CM036, CV_MODEL_DELTA_S) is consistently greater than 80, the expected daily volume of the underlying equity is converted to a notional amount in the issue currency.

PreferredShare:
Estimated total trading volume in number of shares. The LQA model utilizes several reference data features (ex: amount outstanding, industry, age), market data features (ex: trade volumes published to the exchanges) and pricing features (ex: bid-ask spread, and price volatility) to perform a daily calculation of the expected daily volume. The value is displayed as the quantity of shares.

FuturesContract and OptionContract:
Estimated total available daily trading volume. The LQA model considers key features like futures category, currency, days to expiry, open interest, 1-day volume, 10-day price volatility, and moneyness to produce a daily estimate of the total volume that could trade.  The value is displayed as the number of contracts.

Bloomberg normalized (simplified) representation of the trading status of a security, taking into account the Trading Period (RQ063, RT_TRADING_PERIOD) and Exchange Market Status (RQ170, RT_EXCH_MARKET_STATUS) values. Field updates in realtime.

This field will only return a value through BLPAPI (including B-PIPE) for securities that employ the latest version of the security status (version 2). It will not return a value through BLPAPI for securities that are on the earlier version (version 1).

The security status version that is being employed for the security is indicated via the Security Status Version (EX030, SECURITY_STATUS_VERSION/Q1979, SECURITY_STATUS_VERSION_RT) field, which will return a value of '1' (version 1) or '2' (version 2).

The possible values are: 
ABAL - auction order book balancing
AUCT - auction call phase 
CAUC - continuous auction pre-call or call phase dependent on market makers or specialists
CLOS - market closed
HALT - temporary halt from trading
HLTA - temporary halt and auction call phase
INEG - ineligible to trade, e.g. pending listing, delisted, private company, expired, called, etc.
MOC - market-on-close order collection for eventual execution at the determined closing price
MOCB - market-on-close order balancing to try and maximize execution at the determined closing price
NONE - the current status of the security is undefined
NOTR - not presently available for trading
OUT - trading in an out-of-hours trading phase
PHLP - partial halt across the execution venues that form part of the Bloomberg composite, including the primary
PHLT - partial halt across the execution venues that form part of the Bloomberg composite
POST - post-close session
PREO - pre-open session
PRPO - pre-open/post-close session
SUSP - presently suspended from trading
TALC - trade-at-last or trade-at-close trading phase 
TMCB - actively trading, but with market-on-close order balancing operating in parallel
TMOC - actively trading, but with market-on-close order collection operating in parallel
TRAD - actively trading, e.g. continuous trading, mandatory quotation period, etc.
TRAU - actively trading, with an auction call running in parallel 
UNCR - auction uncrossing phase

If you are looking to track the status of a security in simplistic terms, then you make wish to make use of the following generalizations:
- A security has an unknown status when it returns a value of NONE.
- A security is ineligible to trade when it returns a value of INEG.
- A security is closed for trading when it returns a value of CLOS (if Quotation Status/ Quotation Status- Realtime [PR745, QUOTE_STATUS/ RQ180, RT_QUOTE_STATUS] is also equal to 'N').
- A security is available and open for trading (e.g. continuous trading) when it returns a value of CAUC, TMCB, TMOC, TRAD or TRAU.
- A security is available for trade-at-last or trade-at-close order executions only when it returns a value of TALC.
- A security is available for out-of-hours trading when it returns a value of OUT.
- A security is in an auction call when it returns a value of AUCT, HLTA or TRAU. If In Auction Indicator/In Auction Indicator Realtime (PQ654 , IN_AUCTION/ RQ654 , IN_AUCTION_RT) returns a value of 'NO', then the order executions (the uncrossing) has already taken place at the end of that auction call.
- A security is executing orders from an auction call when it returns a value of UNCR (not supported on all markets).
- A security is offering an opportunity to offset an outstanding imbalance from an auction call when it returns a value of ABAL.
- A security is operating a distinct market-on-close (MOC) order book when it returns a value of TMOC or MOC.
- A security is offering an opportunity to offset an outstanding imbalance on a market-on-close (MOC) book when it returns a value of MOCB or TMCB.
- A security is halted or suspended from trading when it returns a value of HALT, HLTA or SUSP. If the value is HLTA then the security is participating in an auction call to facilitate a resumption of trading. For a Bloomberg Composite feed source, the value of SUSP implies that the security has been halted or suspended from trading across all execution venues that form part of the Bloomberg Composite (e.g. Canada Composite, feed source "CN"), unless the Bloomberg Composite feed source has been configured to exclusively emulate the trading status of the execution venue that holds the primary listing (e.g. Australian Composite, feed source "AU").
- A security is halted or suspended from trading across some but not all execution venues that form part of a Bloomberg Composite when it returns a value of PHLP or PHLT; in the case of PHLP the execution venue that holds the primary listing for the security is one of the execution venues for which trading has been halted.
- A security is temporarily unavailable for trading - but not halted or suspended - when it returns a value of NOTR.
- A security is in a pre-trading or post-trading phase (auction calls excepted), but with no trading via the primary market mechanism (e.g. continuous trading), when it returns a value of CLOS (if Quotation Status/ Quotation Status - Realtime [PR745, QUOTE_STATUS/ RQ180, RT_QUOTE_STATUS] is also equal to 'Y'), POST, PREO or POST.

Note that there is a distinction between what we understand to be most likely temporary halts (HALT and HLTA), and what we understand may be longer term suspensions (SUSP). All three values nevertheless represent an unscheduled interruption to trading.

More complete definitions for each of the possible values now follow.

ABAL:
The auction call has concluded, but the market is running a balancing exercise. The mechanics of the balancing phase may vary from market to market, but they typically afford trading participants the option or rebalancing the orders on the book that will execute at the determined equilibrium price. The balancing exercise aims to maximize the quantity that will be transacted following the conclusion of the auction call.

AUCT:
The security is presently in a scheduled auction call. During an auction call, automatic execution is normally suspended for a defined period, during which an equilibrium price and volume is calculated. This equilibrium price and/or volume may or may not be advertised. If it is advertised, it is republished each time it changes. It is often called a theoretical or indicative price/size. It represents the price and quantity that would be executed were the auction call to conclude at that time. The Auction Type/Auction Type - Realtime is available via P1558, AUCTION_TYPE / Q1558, AUCTION_TYPE_REALTIME field.

CAUC:
The security is presently in the pre-call or call phase on a 'continuous auction' market. The 'continuous auction' is distinct from an auction call in that it is not facilitated by, or it is not exclusively facilitated by, a Central Limit Order Book, and it instead depends on a Market Maker or Specialist for executions. For markets that operate periodic auction call uncrossings exclusively on a Central Limit Order Book, a value of "AUCT" will instead be used, together with an Auction Type/ Auction Type - Realtime (P1558, AUCTION_TYPE / Q1558, AUCTION_TYPE_REALTIME) value of "PRDC" (periodic auction call).

CLOS:
The market is closed and it is not possible to trade the security via the market operator's primary trading mechanism. This status would normally be observed before market open and after market close. Markets that observe a trading break between sessions (e.g. a lunch break) would normally have the status of OUT rather than CLOS.

HALT:
Trading in the security has been temporarily halted. This halt may be a manual interruption, whereby the market operator has manually intervened to halt trading in the security, or an automatic interruption, for example when trading limits have been breached during continuous trading or an auction call, sometimes known as a circuit breaker. Note that if a circuit breaker results in a volatility interruption, then the market operator may invoke an auction call to facilitate an orderly resumption of trading. If this is the case then a Simplified Security Status of HLTA will be used instead. If Bloomberg determines that the interruption to trading may be longer term in nature, then a Simplified Security Status of SUSP may be published instead. The reason for the interruption to trading is available via TRADING_HALT_REASON_TYPE / TRADING_HALT_REASON_TYPE_RT field.

HLTA:
A hybrid of HALT and AUCT. Trading in the security has been temporarily halted, but the market operator is operating an auction call to facilitate an orderly resumption of trading. The security is effectively in a hybrid state of both HALT and AUCT. The type of auction is available via Auction Type/ Auction Type - Realtime (P1558, AUCTION_TYPE / Q1558, AUCTION_TYPE_REALTIME). The reason for the interruption to trading is available via Trading Halt Reason Type/Trading Halt Reason Type - Realtime (P1559, TRADING_HALT_REASON_TYPE / Q1559, TRADING_HALT_REASON_TYPE_RT) field.

INEG:
The security is presently ineligible to trade. This may have been determined on the basis of information configured on Bloomberg's instrument database (e.g. security is pending listing or has been delisted), or it may be determined from information received on the inbound market data feed supplied to Bloomberg by the market operator.

MOC:
The security is presently in a market-on-close and/or limit-on-close order collection trading phase. These orders will be executed at the (usually yet to be determined) closing price.

MOCB:
The security is presently in a market-on-close order balancing trading phase. This gives trading participants the opportunity to counteract an imbalance on the market-on-close order book before the orders are executed.

NONE:
Bloomberg presently doesn't have any information that describes the current status of the security. A status of NONE is exceptionally rare, and will only be seen on instruments that have not been fully configured on the Bloomberg instrument databases, and for which there is no information about the security available on the inbound market data feed supplied to Bloomberg by the market operator.

NOTR:
The security is not presently available for trading. This is normally a scheduled/expected transitory trading phase, and it thus does not represent a halt (HALT) or suspension (SUSP) of trading. It is often used by market operators that temporarily freeze the order book or execution of orders on the book while they transition the security from one trading phase to another. It may also be used when a security is between trading sessions on a given day, such as a scheduled lunch break that separates morning trading from afternoon trading.

OUT:
An out-of-hours trading phase is in progress. This status is often used for trading outside of the primary/main market hours, for example pre- or post-session trading, or distinct evening session trading.

PHLP:
Relevant only to Bloomberg equity composite exchange codes (feed sources), e.g. "CN" for the Canada Composite. Indicates a partial halt across the execution venues that form part of the Bloomberg composite, including the execution venue that holds the primary listing for the security. At least one execution venue, excluding the venue that holds the primary listing, has advertised that they have the security available to trade. To determine precisely which execution venues are halted or suspended, the Simplified Security Status value on the equity exchange code (feed source) that represents each execution venue should be consulted.

PHLT:
Relevant only to Bloomberg equity composite exchange codes (feed sources), e.g. "CN" for the Canada Composite. Indicates a partial halt across the execution venues that form part of the Bloomberg composite, excluding the execution venue that holds the primary listing for the security. At least one execution venue, including the venue that holds the primary listing, has advertised that they have the security available to trade. To determine precisely which execution venues are halted or suspended, the Simplified Security Status value on the equity exchange code (feed source) that represents each execution venue should be consulted.

POST:
The market is presently closed, but there is a post-close trading phase in progress. This phase may allow order/quote-entry, deletion and/or amendment, but orders will not be executed until the market re-opens.

PREO:
The market is presently closed, but there is a pre-open trading phase in progress. This phase may allow order/quote-entry, deletion and/or amendment, but orders will not be executed until the market opens.

PRPO:
A hybrid of PREO and POST. The market is presently closed, but there is either a pre-open or a post-close trading phase in progress. This phase may allow order/quote-entry, deletion and/or amendment, but orders will not be executed until the market next opens.

SUSP:
Trading in the security has been suspended from trading. This may be a longer term interruption to trading. If the suspension may be short term in nature, then a Simplified Security Status of HALT may be used instead. If the market operator is operating an auction call to facilitate an orderly resumption of trading, then a Simplified Security Status of HLTA will be used instead. The reason for the interruption to trading is available via Trading Halt Reason Type/Trading Halt Reason Type - Realtime (P1559, TRADING_HALT_REASON_TYPE / Q1559, TRADING_HALT_REASON_TYPE_RT). 

TALC:
The security is presently in a trade-at-last or trade-at-close trading phase. During this phase, special at-last or at-close orders can be executed, which will execute only at the pre-determined last trade from the continuous trading session, or the published closing price (these are often in fact the same price on many markets).

TMCB:
A hybrid of MOCB and TRAD. The market is open for trading (ordinarily the Simplified Security Status of TRAD), but with a market-on-close order balancing trading phase operating in parallel (ordinarily the Simplified Security Status of MOCB).

TMOC:
A hybrid of MOC and TRAD. The market is open for trading (ordinarily the Simplified Security Status of TRAD), but with a market-on-close and/or limit-on-close order collection exercise running in parallel (ordinarily the Simplified Security Status of MOC).

TRAD:
The market is open for trading. This is most commonly a continuous trading phase for markets that operate a central limit order book, but it may also represent a mandatory quotation period for market maker facilitated trading.

TRAU:
A hybrid of TRAD and AUCT. The security is presently in continuous trading (or, for hybrid market maker quote and order book markets, a mandatory quotation period), with an auction call running in parallel. The Auction Type/Auction Type - Realtime is available via P1558, AUCTION_TYPE / Q1558, AUCTION_TYPE_REALTIME. 

UNCR:
The auction call (and auction balancing, if there is such a phase) has concluded, and the orders that have been matched in the auction call are in the process of being executed. During this phase the order book may be frozen in order to avoid any interruptions to the uncrossing process. Note that many market operators do not explicitly advertise an uncrossing phase, and will instead publish the auction call executions either immediately before the auction call concludes, when the Simplified Security Status will still be AUCT or HLTA, or immediately after the auction call concludes, when the Simplified Security Status will represent the subsequent trading phase (e.g. TRAD, TALC or CLOS).

Currency in which the base currency of the underlying currency pair is valued. The base currency is the currency that is quoted in terms of the other. For example, EURUSD is quoted in dollars per euro; the euro is the base currency because the quote is the number of dollars that a euro is worth.

Average price of main market deals on the Moscow Interbank Currency Exchange (MICEX) for equities and bonds. Available once the following criteria are met; a) the number of deals is at least 10, and b) the total value of deals is at least 500,000 Rubles. Field replaced   PX340,ADMITTED_AVERAGE_QUOTE).

On supported markets, this field returns the price of the most recent actual trade that had been eligible to update the latest (last) transaction price trading statistic, i.e. the Last Trade Price.

Whether a trade type is eligible to update the Last Trade Price depends on the market operator and their primary trading facilities or market mechanisms. The rules are usually defined by the market operator or, if they have not defined such rules, by Bloomberg.

For market operators that support automatic execution of orders, the Last Trade Price would typically represent the latest automatic execution on that market.

For quote-driven market operators, the Last Trade Price would typically represent the most recent on-exchange transaction.

For trade reporting venues, the Last Trade Price represents the most recent trade that has been reported and executed on the current trading or reporting day.

If the market operator permits, the Last Trade Price may also be updated by certain off-book or off-exchange transactions.

An 'automatic execution' includes trades executed during continuous trading, an auction call or a pre-open or post-close automatic execution trading phase. An 'automatic execution' excludes off-book, off-exchange trades and official reference prices such as an official close, but includes off-book, on-exchange.

The 'updates last' rules that have been defined by the trading venue for each trade type are respected. Trade types that are not eligible to update the Last Price will also not be eligible to update the Last Trade Price.

The NASDAQ Official Opening Price is the price of the NASDAQ Opening Cross. The NASDAQ Opening Cross is a price discovery facility that crosses orders at a single price at market open. If there is no Opening Cross for a particular issue, then the NASDAQ Official Opening Price will be the price of the first, last sale eligible trade executed in NASDAQ's automated execution system at market open. If there is no automatic execution trade at market open, the NASDAQ Opening Price will be based on the first, last sale eligible trade reported to NASDAQ's Trade Reporting Service and the prevailing NASDAQ Inside quote at the time of the trade. If this trade is outside of the NASDAQ Inside quote then the NASDAQ Official Opening Price will be the NASDAQ best bid or bestoffer, whichever is closer.

 This field does not return data for equity warrants.

 ISO country or territory code for where the Trust is incorporated.

 Bloomberg country or territory code for country of risk of the Credit Default Swap (CDS) reference entity.

 2 letter ISO country code for the quote currency.

To determine precisely which execution venues are halted or suspended, the Simplified Security Status value on the equity exchange code (feed source) that represents each execution venue should be consulted.

PHLT:
Relevant only to Bloomberg equity composite exchange codes (feed sources), e.g. "CN" for the Canada Composite. Indicates a partial halt across the execution venues that form part of the Bloomberg composite, excluding the execution venue that holds the primary listing for the security. At least one execution venue, including the venue that holds the primary listing, has advertised that they have the security available to trade. To determine precisely which execution venues are halted or suspended, the Simplified Security Status value on the equity exchange code (feed source) that represents each execution venue should be consulted.

POST:
The market is presently closed, but there is a post-close trading phase in progress. This phase may allow order/quote-entry, deletion and/or amendment, but orders will not be executed until the market re-opens.

PREO:
The market is presently closed, but there is a pre-open trading phase in progress. This phase may allow order/quote-entry, deletion and/or amendment, but orders will not be executed until the market opens.

PRPO:
A hybrid of PREO and POST. The market is presently closed, but there is either a pre-open or a post-close trading phase in progress. This phase may allow order/quote-entry, deletion and/or amendment, but orders will not be executed until the market next opens.

SUSP:
Trading in the security has been suspended from trading. This may be a longer term interruption to trading. If the suspension may be short term in nature, then a Simplified Security Status of HALT may be used instead. If the market operator is operating an auction call to facilitate an orderly resumption of trading, then a Simplified Security Status of HLTA will be used instead. The reason for the interruption to trading is available via Trading Halt Reason Type/Trading Halt Reason Type - Realtime (P1559, TRADING_HALT_REASON_TYPE / Q1559, TRADING_HALT_REASON_TYPE_RT). 

TALC:
The security is presently in a trade-at-last or trade-at-close trading phase. During this phase, special at-last or at-close orders can be executed, which will execute only at the pre-determined last trade from the continuous trading session, or the published closing price (these are often in fact the same price on many markets).

TMCB:
A hybrid of MOCB and TRAD. The market is open for trading (ordinarily the Simplified Security Status of TRAD), but with a market-on-close order balancing trading phase operating in parallel (ordinarily the Simplified Security Status of MOCB).

TMOC:
A hybrid of MOC and TRAD. The market is open for trading (ordinarily the Simplified Security Status of TRAD), but with a market-on-close and/or limit-on-close order collection exercise running in parallel (ordinarily the Simplified Security Status of MOC).

TRAD:
The market is open for trading. This is most commonly a continuous trading phase for markets that operate a central limit order book, but it may also represent a mandatory quotation period for market maker facilitated trading.

TRAU:
A hybrid of TRAD and AUCT. The security is presently in continuous trading (or, for hybrid market maker quote and order book markets, a mandatory quotation period), with an auction call running in parallel. The Auction Type/Auction Type - Realtime is available via P1558, AUCTION_TYPE / Q1558, AUCTION_TYPE_REALTIME. 

UNCR:
The auction call (and auction balancing, if there is such a phase) has concluded, and the orders that have been matched in the auction call are in the process of being executed. During this phase the order book may be frozen in order to avoid any interruptions to the uncrossing process. Note that many market operators do not explicitly advertise an uncrossing phase, and will instead publish the auction call executions either immediately before the auction call concludes, when the Simplified Security Status will still be AUCT or HLTA, or immediately after the auction call concludes, when the Simplified Security Status will represent the subsequent trading phase (e.g. TRAD, TALC or CLOS).

Exchange Base Price is an official reference price, published by an exchange, that is used to determine the upper and lower trading limits for the current and/or subsequent trading day. It is published before the market has opened each morning, but it may also be published after the market has closed.

In Japan, it additionally represents an "end of day" price, akin to the Official Closing Price. However, because the Exchange Base Price may reflect corporate action adjustments using exchange-defined adjustment factors, as opposed to Bloomberg-defined adjustment factors, Bloomberg does not derive the Official Closing Price from the Exchange Base Price.

The methodology used to determine the Exchange Base Price may vary from market to market. Further details are provided below.

Hanoi Stock Exchange:

Known as the 'reference price'. The price is determined from the previous trading day's close price. Any corporate action adjustments will be taken in to account. For UpCom securities, the reference price will be adjusted after 35 days of no trading.

Borsa Istanbul:

Known as the 'base price'. The price is calculated by rounding the weighted average price of the previous session to the nearest price tick.

Saudi Stock Exchange (Tadawul):

Known as the 'reference price'. If the price is unavailable on a security, then the security will trade without limits on the current trading day.

Japanese Markets (e.g. Tokyo Stock Exchange):

Known as the 'base price'. The price is defined in absolute yen according to the 'previous day's closing price', the last 'special quote' price or the last 'sequential trade quote' price. The price may be adjusted to reflect corporate action adjustments that are to become effective on the next trading day. The price also determines the 'tick direction' against which the first trade on the next trading day will be measured, with reference to the 'up tick' regulatory short sale restrictions.

Korea Exchange:

Known as the 'base price.'  The price shall be the closing price of the previous day.  'Base price' may be adjusted to reflect corporate action adjustments that are to become effective on the next trading day.  The price shall be used as a reference price to determine daily price limit and also used as a reference price of Static Volatility Interruption before the opening price is determined.

Hong Kong Stock Exchange:

Known as the closing auction reference price. This is provided by the exchange between 16:00 and 16:01 of the closing auction session. It is calculated based on the median of five snapshot nominal prices during the last minute of the continuous trading period.

On supported markets, this field returns the price of the most recent actual trade that had been eligible to update the latest (last) transaction price trading statistic, i.e. the Last Trade Price.

Whether a trade type is eligible to update the Last Trade Price depends on the market operator and their primary trading facilities or market mechanisms. The rules are usually defined by the market operator or, if they have not defined such rules, by Bloomberg.

For market operators that support automatic execution of orders, the Last Trade Price would typically represent the latest automatic execution on that market.

For quote-driven market operators, the Last Trade Price would typically represent the most recent on-exchange transaction.

For trade reporting venues, the Last Trade Price represents the most recent trade that has been reported and executed on the current trading or reporting day.

If the market operator permits, the Last Trade Price may also be updated by certain off-book or off-exchange transactions.

An 'automatic execution' includes trades executed during continuous trading, an auction call or a pre-open or post-close automatic execution trading phase. An 'automatic execution' excludes off-book, off-exchange trades and official reference prices such as an official close, but includes off-book, on-exchange.

The 'updates last' rules that have been defined by the trading venue for each trade type are respected. Trade types that are not eligible to update the Last Price will also not be eligible to update the Last Trade Price.

Indicates the type of the current or most recent auction call phase. The possible values are:
CLOS - a scheduled closing auction 
ESDP - an exchange delivery settlement price auction
IPO - an initial public offering auction
ITRA - a scheduled intraday auction
MANU - a manual auction 
OPEN - a scheduled opening auction
PCLS - a periodic closing uncrossing/matching after the continuous trading session for the day has concluded 
PRDC - a periodic uncrossing/matching for securities that are perpetually in an auction
RSME - a special 'resume' auction that facilitates a resumption of trading following a market or technical halt
SCLS - a scheduled closing auction call for a non-conclusive trading session
SOPN - a scheduled opening auction call for a secondary/tertiary/etc. trading session
UNDF - undefined: the inbound market data feed has not specified the type of auction
VOLA - an unscheduled volatility interruption

The 'MANU' Auction Type value is manually instigated by the market operations or surveillance team. An example of where it might be used is when a dependent market maker ceases providing quotes and Market Surveillance initiates a manual auction in order to maintain the instrument in auction until the market maker resumes quoting for the instrument. A manual auction is a standalone event that may be initiated at any time during continuous trading or during (and therefore overriding) a scheduled auction phase (open, close or volatility).

The 'PCLS' Auction Type value is used to represent a periodic auction that takes place after the closing price for the day has been determined. A periodic auction will have several uncrossings, each of which can result in executions at a different price to the earlier published closing price or the previous uncrossing price.

The 'SOPN' Auction Type value is used to represent an opening auction call for a trading session that follows an earlier trading session, such as an afternoon trading session. This opening auction call therefore does not represent the first opening auction call of the trading day, identified via an Auction Type value of 'OPEN'.

The 'SCLS' Auction Type value is used to represent a closing auction call that concludes a specific trading session, such as a morning trading session, but does not represent the final closing auction call of the trading day. A further definitive closing auction call will take place later in the trading day, identified via an Auction Type value of 'CLOS'.

With the exceptions described below, the Official Close is an exchange-calculated and published closing price. Depending on the methodology that is used by the exchange, the closing price may differ from the last traded price.

For the Swiss Stock Exchange (Exchange Codes or Feed Sources of "SE", "SW" and "VX") that have not traded on the current trading day, the field will reflect the value of the most recent official close for that security. This may differ from the Bloomberg Close Price (Q1131, BLOOMBERG_CLOSE_PRICE_RT), which includes reference price ('ref') updates for illiquid securities on days when there are no trades.

For equities, exchange traded funds (ETFs) and convertible bonds admitted for trading on the Japanese stock exchanges (Exchange Codes or Feed Sources of "JF", "JN", "JS" and "JT") the field provides a Bloomberg deriving closing price, which is determined as follows. This algorithm has been formed in conjunction with Tokyo Stock Exchange.
- When the market closes with a trade bearing a Bloomberg condition code value of 'e' (Closing Price), the price of that trade will form the closing price for the day.
- When the market closes with a trade bearing a Bloomberg condition code value of 'z' (Zaraba-Bike) or 'AE' (AM Closing Price) and the market (represented via a Bloomberg bid/ask condition code value) is not in a 'SPEC' (Special Quotation) or 'CONE' (Continuous Quote) state at the closing auction, the 'z' or 'AE' trade price will form the closing price for the day.
- When the market closes with a trade bearing a Bloomberg condition code value of 'z' (Zaraba-Bike) or 'AE' (AM Closing Price) and the market (represented via a Bloomberg bid/ask condition code value) is in 'SPEC' (Special Quotation) or 'CONE' (Continuous Quote) state at the closing auction, the 'SPEC' or 'CONE' bid or ask price will form the closing price for the day.
- When there are no trades at all for the entire trading day, and the market (represented via a Bloomberg bid/ask condition code value) is not in 'SPEC' (Special Quotation) or 'CONE' (Continuous Quote) state at the closing auction, the closing price will be empty/blank.
- When there are no trades at all for the entire trading day, but the market (represented via a Bloomberg bid/ask condition code value) is in 'SPEC' (Special Quotation) or 'CONE' (Continuous Quote) state at the closing auction, the 'SPEC' or 'CONE' bid or ask price will form the closing price for the day. 

On the Bloomberg European Composite (Exchange Code or Feed Source of "EU"), the field provides the Bloomberg Official Close, derived from the last eligible trade from the highest ranked markets that have reported a trade on that day. Markets are ranked according to their market models. Immediate executions (trades) from automatic execution venues are prioritised over manual trades reported from quote-driven markets or manual trade reporting venues. Over-the-counter (OTC) venues, or manual trade reporting venues that are classed as Tier 2 contributors to the European Composite, are not eligible to contribute to the Bloomberg Official Close; only regulated markets and multilateral trading facilities (the Tier 1 contributors) are eligible. The venues that make up the Tier 1 and Tier 2 contributors will vary depending on where the instrument is admitted for trading. A Tier 1 venue may have been classed by Bloomberg as ineligible to contribute to the Bloomberg Official Close owing to extraordinary trading hours, such as a late market close time.

all quotes.description: Diluted EPS from Continuing Operations - Adjusted
all quotes.documentation:
Also known as Diluted EPS from Continuing Operations or Adjusted EPS. 

INDUSTRIALS

Diluted EPS From Continuing Operations:
Excludes the effects of all one-time and extraordinary gains and losses.
One-time charges include: realized investment gains/losses, restructuring charges, non-recurring charges/gains, unusual charges/gains, special charges/gains, reserve charges, large writedowns, spin-off/sell-off expenses, merger expenses, acquisition charges, sale of subsidiary expenses, forgiveness of debt, writedown of goodwill, ESOP charges, and acquired research and development costs.
Includes only those items that are considered to be recurring in nature and part of a company's continuing operations.
Uses weighted average shares figured as if all of the company's convertible securities had been changed into shares of common stock.
When Income before Extraordinary Items minus Minority Interest is negative, diluted shares are not used to calculate Diluted EPS from Continuing because the result is anti-dilutive.  Diluted EPS is the same as Basic.
When Income before Extraordinary Items minus Minority Interest is positive, Diluted EPS from Continuing is valid even if anti-dilutive.
If not disclosed by company, Diluted EPS is same as Basic for US and Canada, blank for rest of world.
If company states there is no significant dilution, assumption is that Diluted EPS is same as Basic.
Not applicable for the UK/Ireland or Australia/New Zealand.

Brazil:
Computed based on the quotation lot of the company. Please refer to PR091, PX_QUOTE_LOT_SIZE for the quotation lot.

One-time charges include: restructuring charges, non-recurring charges/gains, unusual charges/gains, special charges/gains, reserve charges, large write-downs, spin-off/sell-off expenses, merger expenses, acquisition charges, sale of subsidiary expenses, forgiveness of debt, write-down of goodwill.  Includes only those items that are considered to be recurring in nature and part of a company's continuing operations. Includes only those items that are considered to be recurring in nature and part of a company's continuing operations. UTILITIES

Excludes the effects of all one-time and extraordinary gains and losses.
One-time charges include: realized investment gains/losses, restructuring charges, non-recurring charges/gains, unusual charges/gains, special charges/gains, reserve charges, large writedowns, spin-off/sell-off expenses, merger expenses, acquisition charges, sale of subsidiary expenses, forgiveness of debt, writedown of goodwill, ESOP charges, and acquired research and development costs.
Includes only those items that are considered to be recurring in nature and part of a company's continuing operations.
Uses weighted average shares figured as if all of the company's convertible securities had been changed into shares of common stock
When Income before Extraordinary Items minus Minority Interest is negative, diluted shares are not used to calculate Diluted EPS from Continuing because the result is anti-dilutive.  Diluted EPS is the same as Basic.
When Income before Extraordinary Items minus Minority Interest is positive, Diluted EPS from Continuing is valid even if anti-dilutive.
If not disclosed by company, Diluted EPS is same as Basic for US and Canada, blank for rest of world.
If company states there is no significant dilution, assumption is that Diluted EPS is same as Basic.

REITS

Diluted EPS excluding the effects of all one-time charges, extraordinary gains and losses, changes in accounting standards, discontinued operations and early extinguishments of debt.
Includes only those items that are considered to be recurring in nature and part of a company's continuing operations.
Uses weighted average shares figured as if all of the company's convertible securities had been changed into shares of common stock.
When Income before Extraordinary Items is negative, diluted shares are not used to calculate Diluted EPS from Continuing because the result is anti-dilutive.  Diluted EPS is the same as Basic.

If not disclosed by company, Diluted EPS values are the same as Basic for US and Canada.

Ireland:
Before FRS 3, EPS displayed is the Earnings per share figure disclosed by the company in the annual reports.
After the adoption of FRS 3, EPS displayed is essentially the earnings per share from continuing operations. It excludes all items relating to discontinued operations and is computed as follows:

(Income before extraordinary items - Minority Interest - Preferred dvd ) / Average # of shares for EPS

Alternatively it can be calculated as:
{(Net profit + Extraordinary losses (gains) + Tax effect on extraordinary items) - Preferred Dividend} / Average # of Shares for EPS
Extraordinary losses (gains) pretax = Provisions made for discontinued operations +/(-) Net losses (profits) from discontinued operations
+/(-) Losses (gains) from sale of discontinued operations + Extraordinary items, if any, disclosed by the company. +/(-) Goodwill relating to discontinued operations.

Alternatively it can be calculated as:

all quotes.description: Event Quote Aggregated Bid Local Exch Source Rt
all quotes.documentation:
A two-character exchange code (feed source) representing the contributor (market) from which the current best bid price on the composite has been sourced. Where more than one contributor has set the best bid price, a "+" character will be appended.

An example value might be "LN+", indicating that LN and at least one additional contributor share the best bid price. The best bid size will be an accumulation of the best bid sizes from each of those contributors, but the identified contributor will have the largest accumulated best bid size. Where more than one contributor shares the same accumulated best bid size, the earliest contributor to publish that price and size will be identified.

This field is presently only supported on the following Bloomberg Composites:
EZ - European Composite "All Lit"
EP - European Composite "Lit Primaries". Field updates in real-time. The field forms part of the real-time quote event on Server API (SAPI) and the Market Data Feed (B-PIPE). Consequently, it does not provide a value upon initial subscription.

Reports the version of the security status model (business logic) that is employed for the security.
Two security status model versions are available:

'1' - version 1: an earlier primitive set of business rules.
'2' - version 2: a much more advanced and robust set of business rules first introduced in 2012.

The following fields are able supported on both versions. However, many markets on version 1 do not yet provide values in these fields. Comprehensive and robust values are available for markets on version 2:

Trading Period (PR287,TRADING_PERIOD) / (RQ063, RT_TRADING_PERIOD)

It is published before the market has opened each morning, but it may also be published after the market has closed.

In Japan, it additionally represents an "end of day" price, akin to the Official Closing Price. However, because the Exchange Base Price may reflect corporate action adjustments using exchange-defined adjustment factors, as opposed to Bloomberg-defined adjustment factors, Bloomberg does not derive the Official Closing Price from the Exchange Base Price.

The methodology used to determine the Exchange Base Price may vary from market to market. Further details are provided below.

Field updates in realtime.

Hanoi Stock Exchange:

Known as the 'reference price'. The price is determined from the previous trading day's close price. Any corporate action adjustments will be taken in to account. For UpCom securities, the reference price will be adjusted after 35 days of no trading.

Borsa Istanbul:

Known as the 'base price'. The price is calculated by rounding the weighted average price of the previous session to the nearest price tick.

Saudi Stock Exchange (Tadawul):

Known as the 'reference price'. If the price is unavailable on a security, then the security will trade without limits on the current trading day.

Japanese Markets (e.g. Tokyo Stock Exchange):

Known as the 'base price'. The price is defined in absolute yen according to the 'previous day's closing price', the last 'special quote' price or the last 'sequential trade quote' price. The price may be adjusted to reflect corporate action adjustments that are to become effective on the next trading day. The price also determines the 'tick direction' against which the first trade on the next trading day will be measured, with reference to the 'up tick' regulatory short sale restrictions.

Korea Exchange:

Known as the 'base price.'  The price shall be the closing price of the previous day.  'Base price' may be adjusted to reflect corporate action adjustments that are to become effective on the next trading day.  The price shall be used as a reference price to determine daily price limit and also used as a reference price of Static Volatility Interruption before the opening price is determined.

Hong Kong Stock Exchange:

Known as the closing auction reference price. This is provided by the exchange between 16:00 and 16:01 of the closing auction session. It is calculated based on the median of five snapshot nominal prices during the last minute of the continuous trading period.

On supported markets, this field returns the price of the most recent actual trade that had been eligible to update the latest (last) transaction price trading statistic, i.e. the Last Trade Price.

Whether a trade type is eligible to update the Last Trade Price depends on the market operator and their primary trading facilities or market mechanisms. The rules are usually defined by the market operator or, if they have not defined such rules, by Bloomberg.

For market operators that support automatic execution of orders, the Last Trade Price would typically represent the latest automatic execution on that market.

For quote-driven market operators, the Last Trade Price would typically represent the most recent on-exchange transaction.

For trade reporting venues, the Last Trade Price represents the most recent trade that has been reported and executed on the current trading or reporting day.

If the market operator permits, the Last Trade Price may also be updated by certain off-book or off-exchange transactions.

An 'automatic execution' includes trades executed during continuous trading, an auction call or a pre-open or post-close automatic execution trading phase. An 'automatic execution' excludes off-book, off-exchange trades and official reference prices such as an official close, but includes off-book, on-exchange.

The 'updates last' rules that have been defined by the trading venue for each trade type are respected. Trade types that are not eligible to update the Last Price will also not be eligible to update the Last Trade Price.<PR><PR>This field updates in realtime.Field clears at the beginning of each new market day, typically several hours or minutes before the first trading phase commences on each new trading day.

Indication of whether or not the instrument is presently in an auction call trading phase. The field will return y/yes/true (an auction call trading phase is in progress), or n/no/false (an auction call trading phase is not in progress).

The type of the auction call trading phase is indicated via the associated "Auction Type" field: AUCTION_TYPE (P1558) / AUCTION_TYPE_REALTIME (Q1558).

An auction call trading phase will also be indicated via one of the following values on the associated "Simplified Security Status" (PR746, SIMP_SEC_STATUS  / (RQ181, RT_SIMP_SEC_STATUS:
- AUCT (auction call phase)
- HLTA (temporary halt and auction call phase)
- TRAU (actively trading, with an auction call running in parallel)

When the Simplified Security Status field is equal to AUCT, HLTA or TRAU then the In Auction Indicator will also be set to y/yes/true, unless Bloomberg has established that trades representing an automatic execution have been published towards the end of the auction call trading phase. At this time, the In Auction Indicator will be changed to n/no/false to indicate that the uncrossing process has commenced. Thus, a Simplified Security Status of AUCT, HLTA or TRAU corresponding with an In Auction Indicator value of n/no/false can be used to infer that the auction call has actually concluded, even if the market operator has yet to officially transition the security out of the auction call trading phase.

The In Auction Indicator will be set to n/no/false when the Simplified Security Status equals one of the following values, the reason being that the auction call trading phase will in fact have concluded prior to these states, and the definitive equilibrium (indicative or theoretical uncrossing) price represented by PX_THEO (PR089) / THEO_PRICE (RQ089) will have been established:
- ABAL (auction order book balancing)
- UNCR (auction uncrossing phase)

The In Auction Indicator will also be set to n/no/false when the Simplified Security Status equals the following value, as this state represents a trading phase where quote or order execution is dependent on a market maker or specialist, and it is not automatically facilitated via an auction call trading phase on an order book.
- CAUC (continuous auction pre-call or call phase dependent on market makers or specialists)

The Alternative Japanese Evaluation Price is identical to the Japanese Evaluation Price field, PX_EVAL_JAPANESE_REALTIME (RQ047) / PX_EVAL_JAPANESE (PR188) except for the fact that the alternative Japanese evaluation price disregards the exchange base price published after market close, owing to the fact that this may be adjusted for any corporate actions that are to take effect overnight ready for the next trading day. This will however be factored in again on the morning of the next trading day when the exchange base price is republished.

The alternative Japanese evaluation price is calculated intraday and is derived as follows, listed in order of priority (1 being the highest priority). If a higher priority value is not available, then the next value in the priority order will be evaluated.
1. The Last Trade (current day only), unless there is a more recent Special or Continuous Quote (bid/ask) available.
2. The Exchange Base Price published before market close (before the close of the afternoon trading session). This may be the Exchange Base Price that is published before market open.
3. The most recent Japanese Evaluation Price from a prior trading day.

'After market close' and 'before market close' both refer to the close of the afternoon trading session only. For the purposes of the Japanese evaluation price calculation, the afternoon trading session is considered a continuation of the morning trading session.

all quotes.description: Event Trade MMT Level 1 Trade Type Code - Realtime
all quotes.documentation:
Market Model Typology (MMT) Level 1 (Market Mechanism) trade type code for MMT v1.0 and above.

MMT is an evolving standard for describing equity transactions on European markets. It is administered by the FIX Trading Community. For more information on MMT please reference: http://www.fixtradingcommunity.org/pg/group-types/mmt

This field is available only when trade events are received on a market data feed and it should be used in conjunction with the other MMT fields, all of which collectively describe the trade.

This field provides the MMT market mechanism, which defines the fundamental type of mechanism employed by the market in which the trade was facilitated and executed.

The possible values (MMT display codes) are:
CLOB (LB in MMT v4.2 and below) - Central Limit Order Book
QDTS (QB in MMT v4.2 and below) - Quote Driven Market
DABO (DB in MMT v4.2 and below) - Dark Order Book
VOIC (OB in MMT v4.2 and below) - Off Book (including Voice or Messaging Trading)
PATS (PA in MMT v4.2 and below) - Periodic Auction
RFQT (RQ in MMT v4.2 and below) - Request for Quotes
AHHY (AH in MMT v4.2 and below) - Any Other, Including Hybrid (original ESMA definition in RTSs 1 & 2)
HYBR (HS in MMT v4.2 and below) - Hybrid System (revised ESMA definition, replacing 'Any Other, Including Hybrid') [MMT v4.0 and above only]
OTHR (AO in MMT v4.2 and below) - Any Other, Excluding Hybrid (revised ESMA definition, replacing 'Any Other, Including Hybrid') [MMT v4.0 and above only)


More detailed definitions of each of these values now follow.

CLOB (LB in MMT v4.2 and below)- Central Limit Order Book:
A trading mechanism where buy and sell orders are entered onto on an electronically maintained and prioritized order book that automatically matches these orders. The book consists of lit (visible) orders but may also consist of partially or fully hidden orders, such as iceberg or large in scale (LIS) orders. If the order book is in a continuous trading phase, then matching buy and sell orders will be executed and reported as trades immediately. If the order book is in an auction call trading phase, during which orders are theoretically matched for execution at a continuously calculated equilibrium price that ensures the maximum possible executed volume, then the matching orders will be executed and reported at the conclusion of the auction call trading phase. Analogous with the following type(s) of trading system defined under RTS 1 and RTS 2 within MiFID II: 'Continuous auction order book trading system' and - for scheduled auction call trading phases only - 'Periodic auction trading system'.

QDTS (QB in MMT v4.2 and below) - Quote Driven Market:
A trading method by which execution prices are largely determined from buy and sell offer quotations issued by market makers or dealers. Most such systems operate a mandatory quotation period during each trading day, during which registered market makers must display their best buy and sell quotations. The market makers are obliged to transact at those quotations if approached to do so. Analogous with the following type(s) of trading system defined under RTS 1 and RTS 2 within MiFID II: 'Quote-driven trading system'.

DABO (DB in MMT v4.2 and below) - Dark Order Book:
A dark order book offers the similar or equivalent capabilities to a Central Limit Order Book, but only orders set to execute at the (mid-point) reference price interact with like orders via a real or virtual dark order trading facility. Orders are completely hidden which grants the traders full anonymity with Price formation derived from an external reference price.

VOIC (OB in MMT v4.2 and below) - Off Book (including Voice or Messaging Trading):
Trades that have not been executed on a quote-driven or order-driven book, or via a periodic auction or request for quotes market mechanism, are considered to be 'off book' trades. Analogous with the following type(s) of trading system defined under RTS 1 and RTS 2 within MiFID II: 'Voice trading system' and 'Any other trading system not covered by the other trading system descriptions'.

PATS (PA in MMT v4.2 and below) - Periodic Auction:
A trading mechanism where one or more auction calls is the sole method for generating executions and where the auction call is not facilitated by a Central Limit Order Book (CLOB). During the auction call, participants enter buy or sell quotations or orders that may influence an equilibrium price against which the maximum possible volume can be executed at the conclusion of the auction call. The time of the conclusion of the auction call may be predetermined or it may be triggered by specific conditions being satisfied in the market. Analogous with the following type(s) of trading system defined under RTS 1 and RTS 2 within MiFID II: 'Periodic auction trading system'.

RFQT (RQ in MMT v4.2 and below) - Request for Quotes:
A trading mechanism where a quote or quotes are sent in response to a 'request for quote' submitted by one or more members or participants. The quote is executable exclusively by the party initiating the request for quote and this execution is triggered by said party accepting the quote or quotes. Analogous with the following type(s) of trading system defined under RTS 1 and RTS 2 within MiFID II: 'Request for quote trading system'.

AHHY (AH in MMT v4.2 and below) - Any Other, Including Hybrid (original ESMA definition in RTSs 1 & 2):
Any other type of trading mechanism, including a hybrid of some of the above defined market mechanisms and/or price determination processes that facilitated the trade. Analogous with the following type(s) of trading system defined under RTS 1 and RTS 2 within MiFID II: 'Any other trading system' (RTS 1); 'Trading system not covered by the first 5 rows' (RTS 2).

HYBR (HS in MMT v4.2 and below) - Hybrid System (revised ESMA definition, replacing 'Any Other, Including Hybrid'):
A trading mechanism that uses a combination of some of the first 6 of the above defined trading mechanisms at the same time.

OTHR (AO in MMT v4.2 and below) - Any Other, Excluding Hybrid (revised ESMA definition, replacing 'Any Other, Including Hybrid'):
Any other type of trading mechanism, excluding the first 6 of the trading mechanisms defined above or the Hybrid System defined above.

This field should be referenced in conjunction with the other MMT fields in order to obtain a full MMT definition of the trade.

all quotes.description: VWAP Volume for All Exchange Trades (Realtime)

Volume corresponding to VWAP for All Exchange Trades (Realtime) (RQ714, VWAP_ON_EXCHANGE_RT). VWAP for All Exchange Trades (Realtime) (RQ714, VWAP_ON_EXCHANGE_RT) is a trading benchmark calculated by adding up the values of all on-exchange trade transactions (price times shares traded) and then dividing by the corresponding total shares traded for the time period.

This field can be used in conjunction with the VWAP Start Time (PR313, VWAP_START_TIME), VWAP End Time (PR314, VWAP_END_TIME), VWAP Start Date (PR470, VWAP_START_DT), VWAP End Date (PR471, VWAP_END_DT), VWAP Date (PR315, VWAP_DT), VWAP Minimum Price (PR951, VWAP_MIN_PX), VWAP Maximum Price (PR952, VWAP_MAX_PX), VWAP Minimum Size (PR953, VWAP_MIN_SIZE) and VWAP Maximum Size (PR954, VWAP_MAX_SIZE) overrides.

The calculation excludes any off-exchange trade apart from non-trade price quotes like Opening Price, Official Close, Index Point, Aver Price Trade, Current Inside Match Price, NASDAQ First Trade Actual, Far Indicative Clearing Price, Intraday Trade Detail, Market Center Official Close, Near Indicative Clearing Price, and NASDAQ Official Opening Price from VWAP calculations. This field updates in realtime.

Volume corresponding to VWAP (Volume Weighted Average Price) for Automated Trades (Realtime) (RQ715, VWAP_AUTOMATED_RT). VWAP for Automated Trades (Realtime) is a trading benchmark calculated by adding up the values of all order book (electronic) trade transactions (price times shares traded) and then dividing by the total shares traded for the time period.

This field can be used in conjunction with the VWAP Start Time (PR313, VWAP_START_TIME), VWAP End Time (PR314, VWAP_END_TIME), VWAP Start Date (PR470, VWAP_START_DT), VWAP End Date (PR471, VWAP_END_DT), VWAP Date (PR315, VWAP_DT), VWAP Minimum Price (PR951, VWAP_MIN_PX), VWAP Maximum Price (PR952, VWAP_MAX_PX), VWAP Minimum Size (PR953, VWAP_MIN_SIZE) and VWAP Maximum Size (PR954, VWAP_MAX_SIZE) overrides.

The calculation excludes any manual trade apart from off-exchange trades, non-trade price quotes like Opening Price, Official Close, Index Point, Aver Price Trade, Current Inside Match Price, NASDAQ First Trade Actual, Far Indicative Clearing Price, Intraday Trade Detail, Market Center Official Close, Near Indicative Clearing Price, and NASDAQ Official Opening Price from VWAP calculations. This field updates in realtime.

all quotes.description: VWAP Volume for All Lit Trades (Realtime)

This field can be used in conjunction with the VWAP Start Time (PR313, VWAP_START_TIME), VWAP End Time (PR314, VWAP_END_TIME), VWAP Start Date (PR470, VWAP_START_DT), VWAP End Date (PR471, VWAP_END_DT), VWAP Date (PR315, VWAP_DT), VWAP Minimum Price (PR951, VWAP_MIN_PX), VWAP Maximum Price (PR952, VWAP_MAX_PX), VWAP Minimum Size (PR953, VWAP_MIN_SIZE) and VWAP Maximum Size (PR954, VWAP_MAX_SIZE) overrides.

The calculation excludes any 'dark trade' transaction (trade executed off-exchange but reported on an exchange), apart from off-exchange trades, non-trade price quotes like Opening Price, Official Close, Index Point, Aver Price Trade, Current Inside Match Price, NASDAQ First Trade Actual, Far Indicative Clearing Price, Intraday Trade Detail, Market Center Official Close, Near Indicative Clearing Price, and NASDAQ Official Opening Price from VWAP calculations. Indicates the type of the current or most recent auction call phase. The possible values are:
CLOS - a scheduled closing auction 
ESDP - an exchange delivery settlement price auction
IPO - an initial public offering auction
ITRA - a scheduled intraday auction
MANU - a manual auction 
OPEN - a scheduled opening auction
PCLS - a periodic closing uncrossing/matching after the continuous trading session for the day has concluded 
PRDC - a periodic uncrossing/matching for securities that are perpetually in an auction
RSME - a special 'resume' auction that facilitates a resumption of trading following a market or technical halt
SCLS - a scheduled closing auction call for a non-conclusive trading session
SOPN - a scheduled opening auction call for a secondary/tertiary/etc. trading session
UNDF - undefined: the inbound market data feed has not specified the type of auction
VOLA - an unscheduled volatility interruption

The 'MANU' Auction Type value is manually instigated by the market operations or surveillance team. An example of where it might be used is when a dependent market maker ceases providing quotes and Market Surveillance initiates a manual auction in order to maintain the instrument in auction until the market maker resumes quoting for the instrument. A manual auction is a standalone event that may be initiated at any time during continuous trading or during (and therefore overriding) a scheduled auction phase (open, close or volatility).

The 'PCLS' Auction Type value is used to represent a periodic auction that takes place after the closing price for the day has been determined. A periodic auction will have several uncrossings, each of which can result in executions at a different price to the earlier published closing price or the previous uncrossing price.

The 'SOPN' Auction Type value is used to represent an opening auction call for a trading session that follows an earlier trading session, such as an afternoon trading session. This opening auction call therefore does not represent the first opening auction call of the trading day, identified via an Auction Type value of 'OPEN'.

The 'SCLS' Auction Type value is used to represent a closing auction call that concludes a specific trading session, such as a morning trading session, but does not represent the final closing auction call of the trading day. A further definitive closing auction call will take place later in the trading day, identified via an Auction Type value of 'CLOS'.

Field updates in realtime.

all quotes.description: SSE SEHK Connect Quotation Status - Realtime
all quotes.documentation:
Current quotation status of the security (ability to buy or sell) via the Shanghai Stock Exchange (SSE) and the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong (SEHK) Stock Connect program. SSE-SEHK Stock Connect is a mutual market access agreement between the Shanghai Stock Exchange (SSE) and the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong (SEHK).

The possible return values are:

'N.A.' - No value is available, implying that the security is not - and has never been - eligible for Stock Connect.

'BUYS'  - Both buy and sell orders are permitted, provided that the Quotation Status (RQ180, RT_QUOTE_STATUS) is also 'Y'.

'SELL' - Only sell orders are permitted, provided that the Quotation Status (RQ180, RT_QUOTE_STATUS) is also 'Y'.

Note that the field does not indicate order entry restrictions on the domestic order book, and it should thus be used in conjunction with the following fields:
  Quotation Status (RQ180, RT_QUOTE_STATUS)
  Simplified Security Status - Realtime (RQ181, RT_SIMP_SEC_STATUS)

If the Quotation Status is 'N', then the domestic market is not permitting order entry on the security, irrespective of the Stock Connect Quotation Status. The reasons for the Quotation Status of 'N' can be determined via the Simplified Security Status value (e.g. HALT, SUSP, etc.).

It may be possible for a security to be ineligible for Stock Connect but with a Stock Connect Quotation Status of 'SELL' (sell orders permitted), but only if the security had once been eligible for Stock Connect.

The SSE-SEHK Stock Connect Quotation Status is derived from the Daily Quota and Aggregate Quota values. As updates to the Daily Quota are disseminated by the market operator approximately once every 5 seconds, updates to the SSE-SEHK Stock Connect Quotation Status may also exhibit a latency of up to 5 seconds.

Field updates in realtime.

It is dependent on the values provided in Concession Type (DZ487, CONCESSION_TYPE) and Theoretical Concession (DZ486, THEORETICAL_CONCESSION).

Provides the rate used for the Quote Access Payments (QAP) service. FINRA rule 6450 allows broker-dealers to charge access fees that are not displayed in the quotation price. QAP allows using OTC Link subscribers to specify access fees or rebates on a scale of intervalues from -30 through +30, where negative values represent net fee from quote taker and positive values represents rebates. 
See http://www.sec.gov/rules/sro/finra/2010/34-62359.pdf

An index switch is a curve trade that represents selling protection on the first leg and buying protection on the second leg.

Number of original companies comprising the second leg of the credit default swap (CDS) index roll or switch. An index roll is a pair trade between two series of CDSs, where the quote represents selling the older series and buying the newer. An index switch is a curve trade that represents selling protection on the first leg and buying protection on the second leg.

An index switch is a curve trade that represents selling protection on the first leg and buying protection on the second leg.
