Fair value of the credit union's held to maturity investments. Fair value is the amount at which a financial instrument could be exchanged in a current transaction between willing parties. If a quoted market price is available for an instrument, the fair value is derived by multiplying the number of units of the instrument by its market price. Account name: Acct_801. Data is from the National Credit Union Administration's (NCUA) 5300 Call Report.

API-only field providing a bitmask indicating eligibility of a value for updating other fields (e.g. last, high, open, low). The update actions are determined by condition codes.

The field will only be available on trade (MKTDATA_EVENT_TYPE = TRADE) or quote (MKTDATA_EVENT_TYPE = QUOTE) events.

The field returns an integer value, but this must be converted into a binary representation in order to dissect the update actions that apply. If the field is absent from a trade or mid event, then the default update actions had been applied to that event.

The following is a list of the update actions in the bit mask, reading from right to left (0 = ineligible/false; 1 = eligible/true). The default value is shown against each update action.

The list of update actions is identical on trade events and quote events, and it is only the defaults that differ between the two.

The update actions indicate eligibility to update, rather than actual updates. For example, a trade event may have been eligible to update the High, but it may not actually represent the highest trade that day, and it would therefore have left the pre-existing High intact.

The following summaries explain each of the update actions (bit masks). The format is Bit Offset / Default Value / Update Action Eligibility. For example '0 / 1 / Open' indicates that the 'Open' update action eligibility is at bit offset 0 (counting from the rightmost bit) and the default value is 1, i.e. the event had been eligible to update the 'Open' daily statistic.

For trade (MKTDATA_EVENT_TYPE = TRADE) events (the default value is shown to the left of each):
0 / 1 / Open
1 / 1 / High
2 / 1 / Low
3 / 1 / Last
4 / 1 / Open Trade
5 / 1 / High Trade
6 / 1 / Low Trade
7 / 1 / Last Trade
8 / 1 / Cumulative Volume
9 / 1 / Traded Value
10 / 1 / Increment Number of Trades
11 / 0 / Close
12 / 1 / VWAP
13 / 0 / Quote *
14 / 1 / On Book Volume (inaccurate; reserved for future use)
15 / 1 / Off Book Volume (inaccurate; reserved for future use)
16 / 0 / Opening Price
17 / 1 / Last Continuous (inaccurate if LAST_CONTINUOUS_TRADE_PRICE_RT is unavailable)
18 / 0 / Auction Price (inaccurate; reserved for future use)
19 / 0 / Mid *

* = not actually relevant to trade events

For quote (MKTDATA_EVENT_TYPE = QUOTE) events (the default value is shown to the left of each):

0 / 0 / Open *
1 / 0 / High *
2 / 0 / Low *
3 / 0 / Last *
4 / 0 / Open Trade *
5 / 0 / High Trade *
6 / 0 / Low Trade *
7 / 0 / Last Trade *
8 / 0 / Cumulative Volume *
9 / 0 / Traded Value *
10 / 0 / Increment Number of Trades *
11 / 0 / Close *
12 / 0 / VWAP *
13 / 1 / Quote (is this a quote, eligible to update BID/BID_TDY or ASK/ASK_TDY?)
14 / 0 / On Book Volume *
15 / 0 / Off Book Volume *
16 / 0 / Opening Price *
17 / 0 / Last Continuous *
18 / 0 / Auction Price *
19 / 0 / Mid (is this a mid, eligible to update MID/MID_TDY?)

* = not actually relevant to quote events

Let us assume an EVT_UPDATE_ACTIONS_RT integer value of 51215 on a trade (MKTDATA_EVENT_TYPE = TRADE) event. The presence of the field indicates that the default values had not applied. In binary form, 51215 resolves to a set of update actions of:
0000 0000 0000 0000 1100 1000 0000 1111.

This translates in to the following set of eligible update actions that had applied to that event:

0 / 1 / Open
1 / 1 / High
2 / 1 / Low
3 / 1 / Last
4 / 0 / Open Trade
5 / 0 / High Trade
6 / 0 / Low Trade
7 / 0 / Last Trade
8 / 0 / Cumulative Volume
9 / 0 / Traded Value
10 / 0 / Increment Number of Trades
11 / 1 / Close
12 / 0 / VWAP
13 / 0 / Quote (is this a quote, eligible to update BID/BID_TDY or ASK/ASK_TDY?)
14 / 1 / On Book Volume (inaccurate; reserved for future use)
15 / 1 / Off Book Volume (inaccurate; reserved for future use)
16 / 0 / Opening Price
17 / 0 / Last Continuous (inaccurate if LAST_CONTINUOUS_TRADE_PRICE_RT is unavailable)
18 / 0 / Auction Price (inaccurate; reserved for future use)
19 / 0 / Mid (is this a mid, eligible to update MID/MID_TDY?)

all quotes.description: Bloomberg Close Price AM Today - Realtime
all quotes.documentation:
Normalized end-of-session reference price (the "Bloomberg Close Price") for the morning trading session on the tradable security or index. For the definitive normalized end-of-day reference price that represents the full day's trading activity, reference the Bloomberg Close Price Today (Q2187, BLOOMBERG_CLOSE_PRICE_TODAY_RT) or Bloomberg Close Price (Q1131, BLOOMBERG_CLOSE_PRICE_RT).

The derivation method can be identified by querying the Bloomberg Close Method (Q2360, BLOOMBERG_CLOSE_METHOD_RT) field for the security. Possible derivation sources include - where applicable - the settlement price, official close, last price, last trade price, exchange base price and reference price.

This field is only supported on price-quoted securities and indices.

The field will be cleared on each new market day, including public holidays, and will not return a value until the morning session closing price is available.

Field updates in realtime.

Provides the attribute which has been identified that may be relevant to the analysis of whether a security may be quoted under the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) Rule 15c2-11.

This field will only be populated for new issues in the case where SEC 15c2-11 Attribute for Quotation of Securities(DQ206, SEC_15C2_11_ATTRBTE_QUOTTN_SECS) does not return a value.

This information should not be construed as legal or regulatory advice. Users are solely responsible for the selection and use of appropriate parameters, inputs, models, formulas and data for meeting their legal and regulatory obligations.

Indicates whether the issuer of the security has published an periodic collateral report within the past month. Therefore may be relevant to the analysis of whether a security may be quoted under the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) Rule 15c2-11.

Users should determine with their own compliance professionals whether an instrument is quotable under US SEC Rule 15c2-11 and should not rely exclusively on values returned by "SEC_15C2_11" data fields.

Provides the expected borrow cost for a hedge fund, in fee terms, on a given day based on latest day trades. This is a derived rate using S&P's proprietary analytics and data set.

The calculation uses both contributed borrow costs between Agent Lenders and Prime Brokers as well as contributed rates from the hedge fund participants to produce an indication of the current market rate. It should not be assumed that the indicative rate is the actual rate a Prime Broker will quote or charge but rather an indication of the standard market cost.

Provides the expected borrow cost for a hedge fund, in rebate terms, on a given day based on latest day trades. This is a derived rate using S&P's proprietary analytics and data set.

The calculation uses both contributed borrow costs between Agent Lenders and Prime Brokers as well as contributed rates from the hedge fund participants to produce an indication of the current market rate. It should not be assumed that the indicative rate is the actual rate a Prime Broker will quote or charge but rather an indication of the standard market cost.

Provides the expected borrow cost for a hedge fund, in rebate terms, on a given day based on trades in last 7 days. This is a derived rate using S&P's proprietary analytics and data set.

The calculation uses both contributed borrow costs between Agent Lenders and Prime Brokers as well as contributed rates from the hedge fund participants to produce an indication of the current market rate. It should not be assumed that the indicative rate is the actual rate a Prime Broker will quote or charge but rather an indication of the standard market cost.

Forward scale is used to express the precision of FX (foreign exchange) forward points in order to calculate outrights correctly. In FX, forwards are quoted as points off of spot. The forward scale helps compute the outright price (sometimes called the all-in price) that is the actual exchange rate.  If forward scale is '4' (the usual number), then the least significant figure on the points value to the left of the decimal place lines up with the fourth decimal place on the spot. Field updates in realtime.

NASDAQ Official Opening price calculated using both quotation and trade data.  The NASDAQ Official Opening Price will be the price of the first, last sale eligible trade executed in NASDAQ's SuperMontage system at market open. If there is no SuperMontage trade at market open, the NASDAQ Opening Price will be based on the first, last eligible trade reported to NASDAQ's Automated Confirmation Transaction System (ACT) and the prevailing NASDAQ Inside quote at the time of the trade.  Transactions that occur during a crossed market will not be eligible for the NASDAQ Official Opening Price calculation. Field updates in realtime.

Bloomberg-derived time stamp for the current event; always returns in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). Updates only when events are received on the data feed and does not provide initial value. This field updates in realtime, and is supported on events for which the user has a real-time entitlement. It is not supported on events for which the user has a delayed entitlement.

The time is sourced from the Bloomberg Ticker Plant, and represents the time in milliseconds at which the Bloomberg Ticker Plant had published the event. This may be a Local Ticker Plant if the data is consumed via B-PIPE in the same region as the execution venue.

The field is supported on the following event types (MKTDATA_EVENT_TYPE) and sub-types (MKTDATA_EVENT_SUBTYPE) only. The sub-type values are shown in brackets:

  SUMMARY (INTRADAY)

Reports the version of the security status model (business logic) that is employed for the security. This field updates in realtime.
Two security status model versions are available:

'1' - version 1: an earlier primitive set of business rules.
'2' - version 2: a much more advanced and robust set of business rules first introduced in 2012.

The following fields are able supported on both versions. However, many markets on version 1 do not yet provide values in these fields. Comprehensive and robust values are available for markets on version 2:

Trading Period (PR287,TRADING_PERIOD) / (RQ063, RT_TRADING_PERIOD)

Volume corresponding to VWAP for All Trades (Realtime), (RQ713, VWAP_ALL_TRADES_RT). VWAP for All Trades (Realtime), (RQ713, VWAP_ALL_TRADES_RT) is a trading benchmark calculated by adding up the values of all 'trade' transactions (price times shares traded) and then dividing by the corresponding total shares traded for the time period.

This field can be used in conjunction with the VWAP Start Time (PR313, VWAP_START_TIME), VWAP End Time (PR314, VWAP_END_TIME), VWAP Start Date (PR470, VWAP_START_DT), VWAP End Date(PR471, VWAP_END_DT), VWAP Date (PR315, VWAP_DT), VWAP Minimum Price (PR951, VWAP_MIN_PX), VWAP Maximum Price (PR952, VWAP_MAX_PX), VWAP Minimum Size (PR953, VWAP_MIN_SIZE) and VWAP Maximum Size (PR954, VWAP_MAX_SIZE) overrides.

The calculation excludes any non-trade price quote like Opening Price, Official Close, Index Point apart from the Aver Price Trade, Current Inside Match Price, NASDAQ First Trade Actual, Far Indicative Clearing Price, Intraday Trade Detail, Market Center Official Close, Near Indicative Clearing Price, and NASDAQ Official Opening Price from VWAP calculations. This field updates in realtime.

all quotes.description: Limit Up Limit Down Bid Indicator
all quotes.documentation:
Indicates whether the participant quote is executable within the context of the price band for the issue when used on local exchange codes (i.e. UQ, UN, UP, etc.) or describes the limit state of the National Best Bid and Offer with respect to the price band for the issue when used on the composite exchange code (i.e. US).  Possible values:
' ' (space) - Limit Up Limit Down Not Applicable - Bid is Executable
'N' - Local Exchanges:  Bid Price is Above Upper Limit Band Price - Bid is Not Executable; Composite Exchanges:  Indicates National Best Bid is Lower Limit Price Band - National Best Bid is Non-Executable
'L' - National Bid equals Upper Limit Price Band - National Best Bid is in Limit State (only possible on composite exchange codes (i.e. US)).

The Limit Up-Limit Down (LULD) mechanism is intended to prevent trades in National Market System (NMS) securities from occurring outside of specified price bands.  The bands would be set at a percentage level above and below the average reference price of the security over the immediately preceding five minute period.  To accommodate more fundamental price moves, there would be a five minute trading pause - similar to the pause triggered by the current single-stock circuit breakers - only if trading is unable to occur within the specified price band after 15 seconds.  The price band is represented in the Minimum Limit Price (PR507, PX_MIN_LIMIT) and Maximum Limit Price (PR508, PX_MAX_LIMIT) fields.

Identifier that describes the purpose and function of a BLPAPI event (message) on Bloomberg's real-time Enterprise "push" service, //blp/mifid-svcs. This field should be used in conjunction with the Push Event Type (Q3149, PUSH_EVENT_TYPE).

The possible Push Event Type (Push Event Subtype) values are:
- SUMMARY (INITPAINT, INTRADAY, REFRESH, NEWDAY)
- QUOTE (BID, ASK)
- TRADE (NEW, CANCEL, CORRECT, ANALYTICS)

For an explanation of the meaning of the  Push Event Type field values, reference the definition.

Explanations of each of the Push Event Subtype field values now follow.

INITPAINT: provides an initial set of values for the fields that form part of that event. The fields will include those that have been requested in a subscription, together with fields that Bloomberg has determined to be compulsory.

INTRADAY: provides an intraday update to fields in the specified Market Data Service Event Type (RQ620 , MKTDATA_EVENT_TYPE) class (SUMMARY).

REFRESH: provides a refresh of information that may have been earlier communicated. It is generated in instances where Bloomberg has chosen to refresh cached data to help prevent the potential for stale values.

NEWDAY: provides updates that have been triggered by Bloomberg's new market day policies.

BID: the event provides bid (buy offer) data.

ASK: the event provides ask (sell offer) data.

NEW: the event provides information about a new trade.

CANCEL: the event provides information about the cancellation of an earlier published trade.

CORRECT: the event provides information about the amendment of information on an earlier published trade. 

ANALYTICS: the event provides information about value-add calculations pertaining to the trade.

Provides the carbon pricing system under which the company's operations or activities are regulated. The information is sourced directly from the company's response to the Carbon Disclosure Project (CDP) climate change information request.

Net Asset Value (NAV).  Determined by subtracting the liabilities from the portfolio value of the fund's securities, and dividing that figure by the number of outstanding shares. NAV is a per share value. The NAV is the value at which an investor buys and sells shares of a mutual fund.

Values are reported to Bloomberg by a variety of sources, including but not limited to fund companies, transfer agents, official documents, third parties, and other pricing sources.

The pricing source of a fund is stored in Fund Pricing Source (FD046, FUND_PRICING_SOURCE).

Open-End and Hedge Funds:
Returns the net asset value (NAV). If no NAV is available, the bid is returned. If no bid is available, the ask is returned.

Korean non-ETFs:
NAVs are displayed in thousands.
Contributed current last yield of the security. This field updates in real time from pricing sources that contribute this yield data.

Provides the average of the Bid Price (PR002, PX_BID) and Ask Price (PR004, PX_ASK), i.e. (bid + ask) / 2, where both a bid price and an ask price are available to compute the mid price. If only one of the two fields has a current value, then the Mid Price will be set to equal the value of that field. If neither the Bid Price nor the Ask Price has a current value, then the Mid Price will either be a zero (0) or N.A., depending on the service being used to obtain the field value.

The Mid Price is most commonly calculated by Bloomberg on the basis of the supplied bid and ask prices. Alternatively, some pricing sources may publish their own Mid Price calculation, which may be published as the Mid Price. Bloomberg has no control over how such pricing sources may calculate the Mid Price in these instances.

Ticker is a specific identifier for a financial instrument that reflects common usage.  Tickers are not, however, unique to specific exchanges or specific pricing sources. Tickers may change in conjunction with Corporate Actions.

Equities:
Specifies the Bloomberg ticker, which may or may not be an exchange symbol. Often the official ticker is often only confirmed when receiving the official listing confirmation from the exchange (can arrive as late as the day prior to listing).

Corporates, Loans, Preferreds, Municipals, Money Markets, Governments, Mortgages:
Ticker is created by Bloomberg to store and link related securities.

This differs from  the related field Ask OAS Spread (bp) (SP023, OAS_SPREAD_ASK) which is calculated using the user's personal defaults. This field updates in realtime.

pricing sources.description: Bid Option Adjusted Spread by Source - Realtime
pricing sources.documentation: Option adjusted spread (OAS) provided by the pricing source calculated either using a Bloomberg standard (for Bloomberg pricing sources) or the contributor's own calculation method (for outside contributed pricing sources).  This differs from  the related field Bid OAS Spread (bp) (SP021, OAS_SPREAD_BID) which is calculated using the user's personal defaults. This field updates in realtime.
Bloomberg calculated bid yield spread to worst to the benchmark bond. This field will not populate unless the current pricing source delivers spreads.
Bloomberg calculated mid yield spread to worst to the benchmark bond. This field will not populate unless the current pricing source delivers spreads.

Provides the average of the Bid Price - Realtime (RQ002, BID) and Ask Price - Realtime (RQ004, ASK), i.e. (bid + ask) / 2, where both a bid price and an ask price are available to compute the mid price. If only one of the two fields has a current value, then the Mid Price will be set to equal the value of that field. If neither the Bid Price nor the Ask Price has a current value, then the Mid Price will either be a zero (0) or N.A., depending on the service being used to obtain the field value.

The Mid Price is most commonly calculated by Bloomberg on the basis of the supplied bid and ask prices. Bloomberg has no control over how such pricing sources may calculate the Mid Price in these instances.

This field updates in realtime.

Highest intraday price the security traded at in the last 52 weeks, including the current day.  The starting date is determined by subtracting one year from the current day.

Equities:
   Only the data from the default pricing source is used.

Lowest intraday price the security traded at in the last 52 weeks, including the current day.  The starting date is determined by subtracting one year from the current day.

Equities:
   Only the data from the default pricing source is used.
Bloomberg calculated ask yield spread to worst to the benchmark bond. This field will not populate unless the current pricing source delivers spreads.

Either the time or date at which the security last updated. Updates for trades that are eligible to update last price if the security trades. For contributed pricing sources that only provide quotes, quotes may update time. If the last trade occurred today, it will show the time of the trade, otherwise it will show the date on which the security last traded. Field updates in realtime.

Munis:
The date returned is dependent on pricing source settings.

Desktop API:
All values are translated into the user's date and time, per {TZDF<GO>}.

Server API/Managed BPIPE:
Values are returned in GMT/UTC.

pricing sources.description: Last Price as of End of Day
pricing sources.documentation:
End of day value for Last Price (PR005, PX_LAST). End of Day (EOD) fields are populated based on the value of Trading Day End Time End of Day (PQ980, TRADING_DAY_END_TIME_EOD). Until that time EOD fields will return the previous day's close price/value. After that time EOD fields will return today's price/value.

Fixed Income:
When the Pricing Source (PR092, PRICING_SOURCE) is BVAL, today's current prices (not EOD prices) are always used.

Total amount of money invested in the fund, including cash and securities.

Values are reported to Bloomberg by a variety of sources, including but not limited to fund companies, transfer agents, official documents, third parties, and other pricing sources.

When retrieving historic values, the data will be returned in the currency as noted in Total Assets Currency (FD053, FUND_TOTAL_ASSETS_CRNCY) unless a different currency is specified in the history formula.

Display:
This field is displayed in millions (i.e., $10,000,000 is displayed as 10).

The associated currency of this field is stored in Total Assets Currency (FD053, FUND_TOTAL_ASSETS_CRNCY).

The displayed value is effective as of the date stored in Total Assets Date (FD054, FUND_TOTAL_ASSETS_DT).

Korean Mutual Funds:
Fund Total Assets (FD004, FUND_TOTAL_ASSETS) can be found under 'primary fund'. Korean 'Class funds' only display the Class Assets (FD055, FUND_CLASS_ASSETS).
Total number of offers scraped from messages on the current day. Data will be returned only when Pricing Source (PR092, PRICING_SOURCE) is set to MSG1.

Last price for the security.

Equities:
  Returns the last price provided by the exchange. For securities that trade Monday through Friday, this field will be populated only if such information has been provided by the exchange in the past 30 trading days. For initial public offerings (IPO), the day before the first actual trading day may return the IPO price. For all other securities, this field will be populated only if such information was provided by the exchange in the last 30 calendar days. This applies to common stocks, receipts, warrants, and real estate investment trusts (REITs).

Equity Derivatives:
  Equity Options, Spot Indices, Index Futures and Commodity Futures:
    Returns the last trade price. No value is returned for expired contracts.

  Synthetic Options:
    Returns N.A.

Fixed Income:
  Returns the last price received from the current pricing source. The last price will always come from the date and time in LAST_UPDATE/LAST_UPDATE_DT. If there was no contributed last at that time the first valid value from mid/bid/ask will be used. The value returned will be a discount if Pricing Source Quote Type (DS962, PCS_QUOTE_TYP) is 2 (Discount Quoted). For information specific to the last trade see the price (PR088, PX_LAST_ACTUAL), time (P2788, LAST_TRADE_TIME), and date (P2789, LAST_TRADE_DATE) fields.

Returns the last price received from the current pricing source. If last price is not available, then a mid computed from bid and ask will be returned. If either bid or ask is not available to compute mid, the field returns whichever side that is received.

Equity Indices:
  Returns either the current quote price of the index or the last available close price of the index.

Custom Indices:
  Returns the value the custom index expression evaluates to. Since the expression is user defined, the value has no units.

Economic Statistics:
  Provides the revision of the prior release. 

Futures and Options:
  Returns the last traded price until settlement price is received, at which time the settlement price is returned. If no trade or settlement price is available for the current day, then the last settlement price received is provided. No value is returned for expired contracts.
Settlement Price (PR277, PX_SETTLE) and Futures Trade Price (PR083, FUT_PX) can be used instead to return settlement price and closing price respectively at all times regardless of these parameters.

Swaps and Credit Default Swaps:
  Not supported for synthetics.

Mutual Funds:
  Closed-End, Exchange Traded and Open-End Funds Receiving Intraday Pricing from Exchange Feeds:
    Returns the most recent trade price.

  Open-End and Hedge Funds:
    Returns the net asset value (NAV). If no NAV is available, the bid is returned, and if no bid is available then the ask is returned.

Currencies:
  Broken Date Type Currencies (e.g. USD/JPY 3M Curncy):
    Returns the average of the bid and ask.

  For All Other Currency Types:
    Returns the last trade price if it is valid and available. If last trade is not available then mid price is returned. Mid price is the average of the bid and ask. If a valid bid and ask are not available, then a bid or ask is returned based on which is non-zero. If no data is available for the current day, then the previous day's last trade is returned.

OTC FX Options:
  Returns the premium of the option in nominal amount. Returns the price of the option expressed in a currency opposite of the notional currency.

Mortgages:
  Returns the last price received from the current pricing source. If this field is empty for any reason, then last ask is returned and if no ask is available, then last bid is returned.

Municipals:
  Returns the last price received from the current pricing source.

Portfolio:
Net asset value (NAV) as computed in the Portfolio & Risk Analytics function and used for Total Return computations. It is the cumulated daily total returns applied to the user-defined price/value at portfolio's inception date.

Difference between the implied value and the mid price in basis points. Note that this field is calculated every time the data is requested. If the pricing source is set to anything other than BGN or CBBT the date range may automatically be adjusted to a shorter period to provide faster response time.
The Benchmark Short Name used for measuring yield spread to worst. This field will not populate unless the current pricing source delivers spreads.

End of day value for Date Of Last Update (PR371, LAST_UPDATE_DT). End of Day (EOD) fields are populated based on the value of Trading Day End Time End of Day (PQ980, TRADING_DAY_END_TIME_EOD). Until that time EOD fields will return the previous day's close price/value. After that time EOD fields will return today's price/value.

Fixed Income:
When the Pricing Source (PR092, PRICING_SOURCE) is BVAL, today's current prices (not EOD prices) are always used.

Spread that must be added to the spot curve so that a security's discounted cashflows equals its mid price, with each dated cashflow discounted at its own rate. Note that this field is calculated every time the data is requested. If the pricing source is set to anything other than BGN or CBBT the date range may automatically be adjusted to a shorter period to provide faster response time.

The date on which the 52 week high price occurred. For Equities, only the data from the default pricing source is used.
The date on which the 52 week low price occurred. For Equities, only the data from the default pricing source is used.

Total number of shares traded on a security on the current day. If the security has not traded, then it is the total number of shares from the last day the security traded. If an exchange sends official closing price without a volume, the return will be '0'.  If no closing price data is sent by the exchange, the return will reflect the last data received from the exchange. The pricing source in use must be setup to show volume, otherwise the field will return a blank. Field updates in realtime.

This field is currently not supported in Launchpad for indices.  Please use non-realtime field PR013 or approach Equity Index team in Global Data via the Help Desk to find use real-time index volume tickers as an alternative.

  This field supports Credit Default Swap (CDS) overrides for time period and pricing source (PCS).

Fund Total Assets (FD004, FUND_TOTAL_ASSETS) under 'primary fund'. Korean 'Class funds' only display the Class Assets (FD055, FUND_CLASS_ASSETS).

For historical calculation requests, if the pricing source is set to anything other than BVAL the date range may automatically be adjusted to a shorter period to provide faster response time.

If there is no bid at that time but there was a valid ask then NA will be returned. If there is no bid and no ask at that time then the value will match Last Price (PR005, PX_LAST).

   The price at which an investor offers to pay to purchase all or part of a loan.
 
Equities: 
   If the market is closed, this will return the last bid from the last day the market was open. If the market is open, and there is not a bid in the market, this will return 'N.A.'

Swaps and Credit Default Swaps:

 Closed-End, Exchange Traded and Open-End Funds Receiving Intraday Pricing from Exchange 

Feeds:

Fixed Income:

pricing sources.description: Price Display Format Minimum Number of Decimals
pricing sources.documentation: This field returns the minimum number of decimal places to the right of the decimal recommended for display. This field is intended for marketplaces that have a range of security pricing such as sub-penny securities where the minimum increment is much finer granularity than other securities on the same exchange. Additionally, some sources price trades or quotes or different event types in finer increments than other events. This field will describe the minimum number of decimal places to the right of the decimal that should be displayed even if all zeroes. This value can be used to remove trailing zeros from the price display.

pricing sources.description: Bloomberg Spread To Bench Change On Day
pricing sources.documentation: Change on day from the previous Bloomberg-calculated yield spread to worst to the benchmark bond. This field will not populate unless the currency pricing source delivers spreads.
The difference between the current price and the highest price reached in the past 52 weeks. For Equities, only the data from the default pricing source is used.

Current ask price in the market. 

 Equities:
   If the market is closed, it is the last ask from the last day the market was open. If the market is open, and there is no ask in the market, the ask price will be N.A. 

 Fixed Income: 
   This field will return the last available ask price.

Launchpad:
  This field supports Credit Default Swap (CDS) overrides for time period and pricing source (PCS).

API:
This field will return the last available ask price. The value will be cleared when the first bid price of the day arrives in order to avoid misrepresenting the spread for the current day. If the ASK has been cleared upon receipt of a current day BID, Time Of Ask Update (Realtime) (RQ502, LAST_UPDATE_ASK_RT) will display the date of the most recent ask price.

This is the realtime version of Ask Price (PR004, PX_ASK).
Available in EPS MSG1 Data Feed, Desktop & Server API, Data License Back Office.

pricing sources.description: 5 Year Mid CDS Spread on Reference Name
pricing sources.documentation:
Five year credit default swap mid spread based on the user pricing source (PCS) settings. If no market quote is available, the value will be derived through interpolation/extrapolation based on the user credit default swap default (CDSD) settings.

Bloomberg Data License:
A Bloomberg terminal link is required to allow data to return in this field.

The volume weighted average price as calculated by the exchange.  Currently supported for the London, Moscow, Helsinki, Tokyo, Osaka, Nagoya, JASDAQ, Stockholm, Warsaw Stock Exchanges, Korean equities, and for Indian equities, futures, and options.

Currencies:
Supported for Kazakhstan currency securities with a Currency Pricing Source (PX218, FX_PRICING_SOURCE) of KAZ1 (Kazakhstan Mrn), KAZ2 (Kazakhstan Day), and KAZ3 (Kazakhstan Even), and for contributors IMKL (IMKB Large Repo), IMKI (IMKB Interbank), IMKS (IMKB Small Repo), MICE (MICEX Main) and TAKS (Takasbank).

The percentage difference between the current price and the highest price reached in the past 52 weeks.  Futures, Corp, & Govt securities calculate this value as: (Current Px - 52wk Hi)/Current Px.  Equity & Equity Indices calculate this value as: (Current Px - 52wk Hi)/52wk Hi. For Equities, only the data from the default pricing source is used.

A bulk field listing all exchanges on which the security is listed or traded. For bonds the data is sourced from the offering documentation or other information from the issuer or another involved party or if a venue is providing pricing on the security. pricing sources.description: Non Fair Value Net Asset Value
pricing sources.documentation:
Non Fair Value Net Asset Value (NAV). Non fair value NAV is the NAV of the fund determined by local closing prices of the fund's securities, regardless of the local closing time of the fund. For non fair value NAV, the fund does not factor in any after market price changes due to market events.

For example, an internationally-focused, United States-domiciled fund invested in a U.K.-listed security will use the security's price when the U.K. market closes at 11:30am EST when valuing the value of the fund's portfolio at its market close (4pm EST).

Values are reported to Bloomberg by a variety of sources, including but not limited to fund companies, transfer agents, official documents, third parties, and other pricing sources.

Provides the difference between the most recent pricing spread value and the Pre-Announcement Credit Curve Fair Value Spread. This value is calculated using Bloomberg's New Issue Analysis (NIA) function for the relevant issuing entity and debt ranking, utilizing the Bloomberg Valuation pricing source (BVAL) and using Nelson-Siegel-Svensson regression on a yield-to-workout basis.

Eligible bonds must have outstanding amounts exceeding €/$499m or £299m and there must be at least three outstanding bonds with maturities greater than 18 months (and must also include an outstanding security with a maturity that exceeds the tenor of the new issue security) within the debt level to generate the NIA curve. If no curve exists there will be no BNISA calculation.

The Bloomberg calculated asset swap spread, in basis points, being calculated for the security using the Yield & Spread Analysis (YAS<GO>) defaults. The difference between the implied value and the mid price in basis points. There is a one business day lag in the calculation of the most recent (prior to today) historical value; yesterday's value is calculated at approximately 7 p.m. EST (Eastern Standard Time). Where available, this field will use and store realtime spreads. For pricing source BGN only.

Theoretical value of the CDS (Credit Default Swap) index calculated using ISDA (International Securities Dealers Association) hazard rate model to get price of each underlying component and converting the average price to spread.

The value is calculated using an ordered set of contributors by currency which is not impacted by the customer pricing sources selection. The first two contributors in all regions are CMA (Credit Market Analysis) and BBG (Bloomberg). Hence this could cause discrepancy with the data displayed on CDIA/CDIV (the Bloomberg Terminal function), which uses customer pricing source selection, and this field. The value is calculated at the end of the previous trading day.

Total number of shares traded on a security on the current day. If the security has not traded, then it is the total number of shares from the last day the security traded. If an exchange sends official closing price without a volume, the return will be '0'. If no closing price data is sent by the exchange, the return will reflect the last data received from the exchange. The pricing source in use must be set up to show volume, otherwise the field will return a blank. Expressed in units.

Municipal Bonds:
   The total dollar value of all trades for an issue as reported on the last Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board (MSRB) transaction report. The value is scaled by a factor of 1000.

Futures and Options:
   Represents the volume reported on the day the security received its latest settlement or last trade price. CME (Chicago Mercantile Exchange) and CBOT (Chicago Board of Trade) traded securities, volume for Pit/Day session is not available from the exchange during market business hours. The exchange disseminates actual volume/open interest figures at approximately 8am EST, prior to market open the next trading day. For Electronic or Combined sessions, the current day's volume is returned.

Corporate Bonds:
   On FIMMDA:  The total amount traded in the security's currency. The total traded value/total traded amount represents all trade prices, multiplied by the number of bonds X their respective face value of the bond.  The number represents the total amount traded and reported on FIMMDA FTRAC platform managed by CCIL in India.  The value is scaled by a factor of 1000.  Value represented in millions.
   On FINRA TRACE: The volumes are in notional amounts that represent the actual dollar amounts traded. The volume is scaled by a factor of 1000 unless otherwise indicated, and whether the number is alone or with an indicator of scale such as 1(M) = 1000 USD. 

For Equity Indices: Volume is calculated once a day at the end of the day.

MoneyMarketInstrument:
Provides the total volume issued in the security's currency on the primary market on the Fixed Income Money Market and Derivatives Associations Trade Reporting and Confirmation System (FIMMDA FTRAC) platform managed by the Clearing Corporation of India Limited (CCIL) in India. The value is scaled by a factor of 1000. Only applies to Indian Money Markets.

pricing sources.description: Price Display Format Minimum Number Decimals Rt
pricing sources.documentation: Specifies the minimum number of decimal places to the right of the decimal recommended for display. This field is intended for marketplaces that have a range of security pricing such as sub-penny securities where the minimum increment is much finer granularity than other securities on the same exchange. Additionally, some sources price trades or quotes or different event types in finer increments than other events. This field will describe the minimum number of decimal places to the right of the decimal that should be displayed even if all zeroes. This value can be used to remove trailing zeros from the price display. Field updates in realtime.

Provides an alternative official reference price provided by the pricing source. The purpose of the data varies depending on the price source.

For Interbank Offered Rate (IBOR) Fallback tickers, the field represents the latest IBOR Fallback calculation, equivalent to the Last Price (PR005, PX_LAST) value on static data delivery services, such as Data License.

For Nasdaq Nordic Derivatives, this field represents the NASDAQ Margin Price. The Margin Price is the price used for calculating the margin requirements, which should be posted to the clearing house. The Margin Price is based on prices in the market, or it is purely theoretical if no such prices exist.

For TSX and TSX Venture, this is the Imbalance Reference Price. This is the price that determines if a given limit-priced Market on Close (LOC) order can contribute to the MOC Imbalance. LOC orders priced equal to or more aggressively than this price will contribute to the MOC Imbalance.

This field updates in real-time.

Specifies the type of emission allowance.

European Union Allowances (EUA):
Any unit recognized for compliance with the requirements of Directive 2003/87/EC (Emissions Trading Scheme) which represents the right to emit the equivalent to one tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e).

European Union Aviation Allowances (EUAA):
Any unit recognized for compliance with the requirements of Directive 2003/87/EC (Emissions Trading Scheme) which represents the right to emit the equivalent to one tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e) from aviation.

Certified Emission Reductions (CER):
Any unit recognized for compliance with the requirements of Directive 2003/87/EC (Emissions Trading Scheme) which represents the emissions reduction equivalent to one tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e).

Emission Reduction Units (ERU):
Any unit recognized for compliance with the requirements of Directive 2003/87/EC (Emissions Trading Scheme) which represents the emissions reduction equivalent to one tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e).

OTHER:
An emission allowance that does not belong to any of the above sub-asset classes.  Supported for Markets in Financial Instruments Derivative (MiFID) II Approved Publication Arrangement (APA) pricing sources. Field updates in realtime.

pricing sources.description: Event Trade MMT Level 3.2 Trade Type Cd - Realtime
pricing sources.documentation:
Market Model Typology (MMT) Level 3.2 (Transaction Type: Negotiated Transaction Indicator) trade type code for MMT v1.0 and above.

MMT is an evolving standard for describing equity transactions on European markets. It is administered by the FIX Trading Community. For more information on MMT please reference: http://www.fixtradingcommunity.org/pg/group-types/mmt

This field is available only when trade events are received on a market data feed and it should be used in conjunction with the other MMT fields, all of which collectively describe the trade.

This field provides the MMT Negotiation Indicator or Pre-Trade Transparency Waiver, which indicates whether or not the trade had been negotiated or subject to a pre-trade transparency waiver as defined in the MiFID II regulations.

The possible values (MMT display codes) are:
NEGO (N in MMT v4.2 and below) - Negotiated Trade
NLIQ - Negotiated Trade in Liquid Financial Instruments (MiFID II RTS 1)
OILQ - Negotiated Trade in Illiquid Financial Instruments (MiFID II RTS 1)
PRIC - Negotiated Trade Subject to Conditions Other Than The Current Market Price (MiFID II RTS 1)
ILQD - Pre-Trade Transparency Waiver for Illiquid Instrument on an SI (MiFID II RTS 1; SI use only)[deprecated in MMT v5.0]
SIZE - Pre-Trade Transparency Waiver for Above Standard Market Size on an SI (MiFID II RTS 1; SI use only) [Moved to level 3.10 in MMT v4.0]
ILQD,SIZE - Where both ILQD and SIZE apply (MiFID II RTS 1; SI use only). [deprecated in MMT v4.0]
NLTS - OTC Trade Larger Than LIS Brought Onto a Venue (added in MMT v4.0)

* the consensus view is that this is an illogical combinations of MiFID II trade flags, but it is listed as an option for those pricing sources that wish to define both for a given trade. The consensus view is that of industry participants, including the FIX MiFID Transparency Working Group and the FIX Market Model Typology Steering and Technical Committees.

If the field is empty or absent from a trade event that otherwise provides other MMT fields and values, then a value of 'No Negotiated Trade' can be assumed. There is no MMT display code for this default value.

More detailed definitions of each of these values now follow.

NEGO (N in MMT v4.2 and below) - Negotiated Trade:
A bilateral negotiated trade that is not subject to pre-trade transparency on the market through which it has been facilitated and/or reported. To be used only where one of the following definitions does not apply for:
- 'Negotiated Trade in Liquid Financial Instruments';
- 'Negotiated Trades in Illiquid Financial Instruments'; and
- 'Negotiated Trade Subject to Conditions Other Than The Current Market Price'.

NLIQ - Negotiated Trade in Liquid Financial Instruments (MiFID II RTS 1):
Transactions executed in accordance with Article 4(1)(b)(i) of Regulation (EU) No 600/2014.

OILQ - Negotiated Trade in Illiquid Financial Instruments (MiFID II RTS 1):
Transactions executed in accordance with Article 4(1)(b)(ii) of Regulation (EU) No 600/2014.

PRIC - Negotiated Trade Subject to Conditions Other Than The Current Market Price (MiFID II RTS 1):
Transactions executed in accordance with Article 4(1)(b)(iii) of Regulation EU) No 600/2014 and as set out in Article 6.

ILQD - Pre-Trade Transparency Waiver for Illiquid Instrument on an SI (MiFID II RTS 1; SI use only): [deprecated in MMT v5.0]
Transactions in illiquid instruments as determined in accordance with Article s 1 to 9 of Commission Delegated Regulation [MiFIR Level 2] executed on a systematic internaliser.

SIZE - Pre-Trade Transparency Waiver for Above Standard Market Size on an SI (MiFID II RTS 1; SI use only):
Transactions executed on a systematic internaliser where the size of the incoming order was above the standard market size as determined in accordance with Article 11. [Moved to level 3.10 in MMT v4.0]

ILQD,SIZE - Where both ILQD and SIZE apply (MiFID II RTS 1; SI use only). [deprecated in MMT v4.0]:
A combination of the "ILQD" and "SIZE" flags defined above.

NLTS - OTC Trade Larger Than LIS Brought Onto a Venue (added in MMT v4.0):

No Negotiated Trade:
A trade for which none of the above definitions apply, and therefore does not represent a negotiated transaction per the terms described therein.

This field should be referenced in conjunction with the other MMT fields in order to obtain a full MMT definition of the trade.

Field updates in real time and forms part of the trade events on SAPI and B-PIPE. As the field is defined as a component of a trade event on SAPI and B-PIPE, it does not support an initial value upon first subscription.

pricing sources.description: Event Trade MMT Level 4.1 Trade Type Cd - Realtime
pricing sources.documentation:
Market Model Typology (MMT) Level 4.1 (Post-Trade Deferral Reason) trade type code for MMT v3.01 and above.

MMT is an evolving standard for describing equity transactions on European markets. It is administered by the FIX Trading Community. For more information on MMT please reference: http://www.fixtradingcommunity.org/pg/group-types/mmt

This field provides the MMT Post-Trade Deferral Reason, which indicates whether or not the publication of the trade had been deferred at source and, if required by the MiFID II regulations, the reason for the deferral.

The possible values (MMT display codes) are:
NIPM (NI in MMT v4.2 and below) - Non-Immediate Publication
LRGS - Non-Immediate Publication: Deferral for 'Large in Scale' (MiFID II RTS 1 and 2)
ILQD - Non-Immediate Publication: Deferral for 'Illiquid Instrument' (MiFID II RTS 2) - [moved to MMT Level 4.3 in MMT v4.0]
SIZE - Non-Immediate Publication: Deferral for 'Size Specific' (MiFID II RTS 2) - [moved to MMT Level 4.3 in MMT v4.0]
ILQD,SIZE - Where both ILQD and SIZE apply (MiFID II RTS 2) - [deprecated in MMT v4.0 and above]
ILQD,LRGS - Where both ILQD and LRGS apply (MiFID II RTS 2) - [deprecated in MMT v4.0 and above]
MLF1 - Non-Immediate Publication: Deferral for Medium Size Liquid Market (MiFID II RTS 2)
MIF2 - Non-Immediate Publication: Deferral for Medium Size Illiquid Market (MiFID II RTS 2)
LLF3 - Non-Immediate Publication: Deferral for Large Size Liquid Market (MiFID II RTS 2)
LIF4 - Non-Immediate Publication: Deferral for Large Size Illiquid Market (MiFID II RTS 2)
VLF5 - Non-Immediate Publication: Deferral for Very Large Size Liquid Market (MiFID II RTS 2)
VIF5 - Non-Immediate Publication: Deferral for Very Large Size Illiquid Market (MiFID II RTS 2)
DEFF - Non-Immediate Publication: Deferral for ETCs, ETNs, SFPs, Emission Allowances (MiFID II RTS 2)

* the consensus view is that these are illogical combinations of MiFID II trade flags, but they are listed as options for those pricing sources that wish to define both for a given trade. The consensus view is that of industry participants, including the FIX MiFID Transparency Working Group and the FIX Market Model Typology Steering and Technical Committees.

If the field is empty or absent from a trade event that otherwise provides other MMT fields and values, then a value of 'Immediate Publication' can be assumed. There is no MMT display code for this default value.

More detailed definitions of each of these values now follow.
NIPM (NI in MMT v4.2 and below) - Non-Immediate Publication:
A trade that is not being reported to the market immediately following execution. This would encapsulate 'late' trades that legally should have been reported immediately but had not been owing to a technical or procedural issue, and 'deferred publication' trades that are legally eligible to be subject to deferred publication, for example those derived from large in scale orders.

LRGS - Non-Immediate Publication: Deferral for 'Large in Scale' (MiFID II RTS 1 and 2):
RTS 1: Transactions that are large in scale compared with normal market size for which deferred publication is permitted under Article 14.
RTS 2: Transactions executed under the post-trade large in scale deferral.

ILQD - Non-Immediate Publication: Deferral for 'Illiquid Instrument' (MiFID II RTS 2):
Transactions executed under the deferral for instruments for which there is not a liquid market. [moved to MMT Level 4.3 in MMT v4.0]

SIZE - Non-Immediate Publication: Deferral for 'Size Specific' (MiFID II RTS 2):
Transactions executed under the post-trade size specific to the instrument deferral. [moved to MMT Level 4.3 in MMT v4.0]

MLF1 - Non-Immediate Publication: Deferral for Medium Size Liquid Market (MiFID II RTS 2):
Transactions in bonds benefiting from a deferral applicable to transactions of a medium size in a financial instrument for which there is a liquid market.

MIF2 - Non-Immediate Publication: Deferral for Medium Size Illiquid Market (MiFID II RTS 2):
Transactions in bonds benefiting from a deferral applicable to transactions of a medium size in a financial instrument for which there is not a liquid market.

LLF3 - Non-Immediate Publication: Deferral for Large Size Liquid Market (MiFID II RTS 2):
Transactions in bonds benefiting from a deferral applicable to transactions of a large size in a financial instrument for which there is a liquid market.

LIF4 - Non-Immediate Publication: Deferral for Large Size Illiquid Market (MiFID II RTS 2):
Transactions in bonds benefiting from a deferral applicable to transactions of a very large size in a financial instrument for which there is a liquid market.

VLF5 - Non-Immediate Publication: Deferral for Very Large Size Liquid Market (MiFID II RTS 2):
Transactions in bonds benefiting from a deferral applicable to transactions of a large size in a financial instrument for which there is not a liquid market.

VIF5 - Non-Immediate Publication: Deferral for Very Large Size Illiquid Market (MiFID II RTS 2):
Transactions in bonds benefiting from a deferral applicable to transactions of a very large size in a financial instrument for which there is not a liquid market.

DEFF - Non-Immediate Publication: Deferral for ETCs, ETNs, SFPs, Emission Allowances (MiFID II RTS 2):
Transactions in ETCs, ETNs, SFPs and emission allowances, which benefit from a deferred publication.

Immediate Publication:
A trade that has been reported to the market immediately following execution.

This field should be referenced in conjunction with the other MMT fields in order to obtain a full MMT definition of the trade.

Field updates in real time and forms part of the trade events on SAPI and B-PIPE. As the field is defined as a component of a trade event on SAPI and B-PIPE, it does not support an initial value upon first subscription.
